# Map / Navigation Survey — Run B: Email Reminders and Delegate Configurations

Corpus: SAP `2026_08`, Professional Edition, crawled 2026-08-29.
Both guide directories searched at equal weight. **Result of that sweep: every file that
documents either page lives in `concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/`. The
tools-guides directory contributes ZERO source files to either page** — its five
delegate-matching files are end-user proxy/delete-invoice topics and a condition-editor
field catalogue, none of which describe either admin page. That is a positive finding,
not a skipped search.

No URL is published for either page. The corpus publishes no `.asp` URL anywhere, and
`navPath` is the identifier for both.

---

## 1. Email Reminders

### 1.1 Page identity — CONFIRMED

Email Reminders is its own admin page, not a tab of Workflows. Three independent
structural facts, each grounded:

1. **Its own menu destination**, in the same syntactic slot as six already-built pages:
   `"From the Invoice Processing Admin navigation menu, choose Email Reminders."`
   followed by `"The Email Reminders page appears."`
   (`access-email-reminders-96f3ca18.md`).
2. **Its own two-tab object surface** — Rules and Email Reminders, both attested with the
   phrase "of the Email Reminders page".
3. **Its own object model with two object types and full CRUD on each** — reminder RULES
   (create / copy / edit / delete, four dedicated topics) and email REMINDERS (create /
   copy / edit / delete, four more). A rule must exist before a reminder can use it.

I explicitly do NOT rest page-hood on the role gate. The recon brief already corrected
that: `Invoice Configuration administrator (Restricted)` gates NINE surfaces in this
corpus — measured, `grep -rln "Invoice Configuration administrator (Restricted)"` over
both directories returns exactly 9 files (`email-reminders-tool-8b2c8a11.md`,
`overview-8b2edfd0.md`, `required-roles-1f2a20f6.md`,
`set-a-default-shipping-and-billing-address-f772bed1.md`,
`shipping-configuration-and-shipping-terms-3429ee14.md`, plus four tools-guides files).
The gate is real; it is not a discriminator.

### 1.2 Navigation

Two documented idioms, and they must both be recorded:

| navPath | quote | file |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Administration > Invoice | `Select Administration  Invoice.` | access-email-reminders-96f3ca18.md |
| Administration > Invoice > Invoice Processing Admin > Email Reminders | "From the Invoice Processing Admin navigation menu, choose Email Reminders." | access-email-reminders-96f3ca18.md |
| (landing confirmation) | "The Email Reminders page appears." | access-email-reminders-96f3ca18.md |
| Administration > Invoice > Email Reminders (middle node UNATTESTED in this sentence) | `The Email Reminders tool, located in Administration  Invoice, allows a Global and Group Configuration administrator to create, edit, and delete email reminders by group. Group Configuration administrators can only create, edit, and delete email reminders for the groups to which they have access permissions.` | email-reminders-tool-8b2c8a11.md |

**⚠ NBSP, MEASURED.** Both of the sentences above that name `Administration` contain
**NO `>` glyph at all**. The separators are two consecutive U+00A0 characters:

- `access-email-reminders-96f3ca18.md`, 2 NBSP, step 1 reads
  `Select Administration<U+00A0><U+00A0>Invoice.`
- `email-reminders-tool-8b2c8a11.md`, 2 NBSP, the role sentence reads
  `... located in Administration<U+00A0><U+00A0>Invoice, allows a Global and Group ...`

`create-email-reminders-604c4a46.md` (14 NBSP) and `create-reminder-rules-b0a7fac5.md`
(14 NBSP) carry theirs inside the **Editable By** descriptions
(`Global Group<U+00A0><U+00A0>United States`), not in a nav sentence.

**Emission decision for the structured object.** `bin/validate-graph.py` normalises NBSP
to a space before comparing, so a retyped quote passes validation and lands permanently
wrong — a nav string a Chromium driver can never match. I measured my own emission
fidelity twice against these two files and it was **not reliable** (one attempt produced
U+00A0, one produced U+0020, same intent). Rather than gamble a silently-wrong string
into the graph, the two NBSP sentences are **NOT emitted as sourceQuotes**. Instead:

- the `Administration > Invoice` first segment is attested by the deliberately
  boundary-truncated verbatim `"Select Administration"` (grep -F verified, 1 hit), cut
  exactly where the first U+00A0 begins;
- the role gate is attested by the ASCII-clean tail
  `"allows a Global and Group Configuration administrator to create, edit, and delete email reminders by group."`
  (grep -F verified, 1 hit).

A correction pass that can write bytes directly should replace both with the full
sentences shown above, inserting U+00A0 U+00A0 where this document writes
`<U+00A0><U+00A0>`. **Do not retype them by hand.**

The `(left menu)` census misses this page entirely — its access topic uses the other
phrasing. That is why four of six recon sweeps failed to find it.

### 1.3 Tabs

Two tabs: **Rules** and **Email Reminders**. Every attestation binds the tab to "the Email
Reminders page":

- "On the Rules tab of the Email Reminders page, create any specific email rules for the reminder" (configuration-process-8b2c271f.md)
- "On the Email Reminders tab of the Email Reminders page, create a new configuration." (configuration-process-8b2c271f.md) — emitted as `tabsSourceQuote`
- "On the Email Reminders page, select the Rules tab." (create-reminder-rules-b0a7fac5.md)
- "The rules are set up in the Rules tab of the Email Reminders page." (before-you-begin-448d2513.md)

Alias for the Rules tab found in the roster itself: "The Email Reminder Rules section of
this tool is used to create any new rules." (create-email-reminders-604c4a46.md).

### 1.4 Child surfaces — MODALS AND A WIZARD, NOT PAGES

This page has exactly the same label-drift shape as Delegate Configurations, and the
answer is the same:

- "Choose New to open the Email Reminder window." (create-email-reminders-604c4a46.md)
- "Below is an example of how those options are used on the Add Email Reminder page." (email-message-replacement-tokens-c9cc4af4.md)
- "then the Edit Email Reminder page will be read-only." (edit-email-reminders-2a2638ad.md)
- "The New Reminder Rule - Step 1 page appears." / "The Conditions - Step 2 page appears." (create-reminder-rules-b0a7fac5.md)

Three names for one reminder editor; two more for a two-step rule wizard. **None is a
page node.** No menu destination, no distinct role gate, no distinct object — they are
modal editors over the two objects the page already owns. The two "Step 1 / Step 2" pages
are the Workflows General / Steps / Step Rules precedent exactly.

### 1.5 Boundary against Workflows > Email Notifications (ALREADY BUILT)

The single easiest collapse error in this domain, and there is a concrete field-name
collision to prove it. The built graph already carries, on `page.workflows`:
`field.workflows.email-notification-display-as-from` ("Display as From") and
`field.workflows.email-subject` ("Email Subject"), both from
`add-an-email-notification-c237a2de.md` / `modify-an-email-notification-a6e5f4ba.md`.
**Email Reminders has its own "Display as From" and its own "Email Subject", from
`create-email-reminders-604c4a46.md`.** They are different controls on different pages.
Do not re-home, do not merge, do not "dedupe by label".

Notifications = event-driven templates authored inside Workflows and assigned to a
workflow object. Reminders = interval-driven nag emails with their own rule engine, on
their own page, assigned by GROUP.

**Verified against the built graph (23 pages / 617 fields):** not one built field cites
`create-email-reminders-604c4a46.md`, `create-reminder-rules-b0a7fac5.md`,
`access-email-reminders-96f3ca18.md`, `email-reminders-tool-8b2c8a11.md`,
`configuration-process-8b2c271f.md`, `overview-8b2c769e.md`,
`pre-defined-rules-220a1fe7.md` or `before-you-begin-448d2513.md`. The roster is clean to
take. The six already-mined files in the broad sweep
(`work-with-the-steps-page-fab249d1.md`, `add-groups-ec5d8d8b.md`,
`overview-8b2edfd0.md`, `workflow-667cee21.md`,
`about-vendor-approval-workflow-step-and-timeout-b3d1bd2c.md`,
`email-message-replacement-tokens-c9cc4af4.md`) are corroboration/dependency sources only.

### 1.6 Role gates and a role PARTITION worth recording

- "The Email Reminders tool is visible if you have the Invoice Configuration administrator (Restricted) role." (email-reminders-tool-8b2c8a11.md)
- "allows a Global and Group Configuration administrator to create, edit, and delete email reminders by group." (email-reminders-tool-8b2c8a11.md)
- "Group Configuration administrators can only create, edit, and delete email reminders for the groups to which they have access permissions." (email-reminders-tool-8b2c8a11.md)
- "Group administrators can only create email reminder rules if given \"create\" rights." (create-reminder-rules-b0a7fac5.md)

`(Restricted)` and `Global and Group Configuration administrator` appear in the SAME file
and are NOT a contradiction — one is visibility, the other is what the admin may do.

**Hard cross-page constraint:** "The Group Configurations tool is not visible if you have
the Invoice Configuration administrator (Restricted) role." (`overview-8b2edfd0.md`).
So the very admin who can reach Email Reminders CANNOT reach Group Configurations — yet
the Applies to / Editable By fields assign reminders BY GROUP. Emit that as a dependency
constraint on the group-assignment edge, not as a field.

### 1.7 The contradiction to emit (Reminder Type)

Two rosters, same control name, two different option lists, and the shared option is
defined incompatibly. Both quotes grep -F verified:

| create-email-reminders-604c4a46.md (Email Reminders tab) | create-reminder-rules-b0a7fac5.md (Rules tab) |
| --- | --- |
| "Approval Request - Payment Request: When a cash advance request has a status of Pending Approval." | "Approval Request - Payment Request: When an invoice has a status of Pending Approval." |
| "Approval Request - Vendor Request: When a vendor-based invoice has a status of Pending Approval." | "Approval Request - Payment Vendor: When a vendor-based invoice has a status of Pending Approval." |
| "Payment Request: ..." | "Payment Request: ..." |

`Approval Request - Vendor Request` appears ONLY on the reminder side;
`Approval Request - Payment Vendor` ONLY on the rule side. Record BOTH value sets with
distinct context and ONE contradiction node. Do not reconcile — do not pick "cash advance
request" or "invoice" as the true gloss.

### 1.8 Three guaranteed name collisions WITHIN this page

`duplicate-field-name` is a hard validator error scoped PER PAGE, not per tab. The Rules
tab roster has exactly three field rows — Name, Reminder Type, Editable By — and all three
labels are also standalone table cells on the Email Reminders tab roster. They are
different controls with different descriptions (rule vs. reminder wording, and genuinely
disagreeing Reminder Type lists). Prefix the rule side (`rule_name`,
`rule_reminder_type`, `rule_editable_by`), keep the reminder side bare, put the tab in
notes on both. **Do not merge them to duck the error.**

### 1.9 Census — the trap, measured

`grep -c "^| "` is worthless here. Measured across the 25-file sweep, only four files
return anything on the naive anchor, and the real roster returns **zero**:

| file | bytes | `^\| ` | `^\s*\|` cell-openers | TRUE field rows |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| create-email-reminders-604c4a46.md | 10,163 | **0** | **49** | **15** |
| create-reminder-rules-b0a7fac5.md | 3,979 | 0 | 13 | **3** |
| email-message-replacement-tokens-c9cc4af4.md | 2,796 | 6 | 21 | **4** (%1% %2% %3% %4%) |
| email-reminders-8b2caa99.md | 3,921 | 31 | 91 | **0 — revision history, ~29 dated entries** |

**49 IS NOT A ROW COUNT.** SAP writes every table cell on its own line. The fifteen true
rows on `create-email-reminders-604c4a46.md`, extracted mechanically, are: Name, Reminder
Type, Reminder Rule, Frequency, Number of Days, Specific days, Display as From, Email
Subject, Email Message, Copy to Approver, Copy to Employee, Copy to Email Address,
Editable By, Applies to, Active. An extractor that believes 49 will hunt for 34 fields
that do not exist.

**Zero raw `<table>` HTML anywhere in the 25-file set** (measured: `<table` count 0 in
every file). Total set 62,693 B across 25 files.

### 1.10 A known graph gap this page closes

`vset.g3.unnamed.email-message-replacement-tokens-the-4-row-variable-label-na` is
currently orphaned with `knownGap: true`; its own note says what would fix it is "an
Email Reminders page node that owns this table properly". The file is
`email-message-replacement-tokens-c9cc4af4.md`; its cell-opener count is 21 and its true
content is exactly FOUR tokens — %1% Logon URL, %2% User Name, %3% Number of Records, %4%
List of Records. The existing node already carries those four. **RE-HOME that 4-value set
onto this page. Do not hunt for 17 more tokens that do not exist.** Note that
`page.purchase-order-configuration` and
`field.purchase-order-configuration.default-email-subject-when-transmitting-purchase-orders`
also reference this file — leave those alone; the value set is the only thing moving.

### 1.11 Scheduling is NOT a control on this page

"Scheduling email reminders is done in the Import/Extract Administrator tool and is
performed by SAP Concur staff." and "Scheduling requires you to submit a service request
to SAP Concur support." (`configuration-process-8b2c271f.md`), corroborated by
`scheduling-email-reminders-8b2ceaea.md`. Emit as a dependency / step rationale pointing
at the unbuilt Import/Extract Administrator surface. A driver cannot click it. Same for
localisation string extraction (`localizing-email-reminder-text-8b2cc1b0.md`).

### 1.12 "Rules tab" names THREE surfaces — say which you mean

1. **Email Reminders > Rules** (this page).
2. **Purchase Order Matching Rules > Rules** (already built, `page.purchase-order-matching-rules`).
3. **Workflows Step Rules** wizard page (ruled NOT a page).

### 1.13 documentedBasis: **rich**

Justification: two field-level rosters in two separate topics (15 rows + 3 rows), a
fully enumerated 4-row token catalogue, enumerated value lists on Reminder Type (×2,
contradictory), Frequency (5 options), Copy to Approver / Copy to Employee / Active
(Yes/No stated explicitly in prose — and note the Yes/No is DOCUMENTED here, not
inferred), Editable By (Global Group / named groups), plus dedicated topics for
localisation, pre-defined rules, prerequisites and the configuration process, plus eight
CRUD procedure topics. Real gaps remain: the Conditions - Step 2 condition editor is only
step-listed (Data Object, Field/Value, Operator) and never enumerated for reminders, and
the pre-defined rule set is given as two named rules with no configuration surface.
`coverageGuess: good`. `uiVariant: undifferentiated` — the only UI-variant language in the
set is 2014/2015 revision-history boilerplate ("Added information about the two user
interfaces", "Updated the images to the enhanced UI"), which is history, not a live
variant.

## 2. Delegate Configurations

### 2.1 Page identity — CONFIRMED, and a SIBLING of Workflows, never under it

Grounded facts:

- Its own left-menu destination: "Select Delegate Configurations (left menu) , the Delegate Configurations page appears." (`access-and-view-payment-delegate-configurations-8ed1298f.md`)
- Its own tool name: "To access the Delegate Configurations tool:" (same file)
- Its own two tabs (Invoice, Purchase Request) and its own object (a delegate configuration) with full CRUD across four dedicated topics.
- Independent corroboration already written into the graph: `dep.g1.059` targets
  `{page: "Delegate Configurations", field: "Delegate Configuration", resolved: false}`,
  authored by a Group 1 agent who had no roster.
- Further corroboration: the built `page.workflows` node's own notes already say the
  "Select the Invoice or Purchase Request tab." sentence "is DELEGATE CONFIGURATIONS (a
  Run B page)" — Run A explicitly declined to absorb it.

The corpus NEVER places this page under Workflows — measured, zero hits in the 12
delegate-named admin files. It is squarely approval configuration and it cross-references
the built Workflows Authorized Approvers surface via
"Restrict approvers to those with equal or higher authorized approver limit", but that is
a cross-page dependency, not a home.

### 2.2 Navigation — the OTHER idiom, and a verbatim trap

This page uses the plain `(left menu)` idiom; the Invoice Processing Admin middle node is
**never mentioned** for it. Treat the middle segment as UNATTESTED, not absent. Do not
copy the Email Reminders idiom onto this page.

**⚠ THE STRAY SPACE BEFORE THE COMMA IS VERBATIM**: `(left menu) , the`. Do not tidy it.
Verified byte-exact (1 hit).

**NBSP: this page is CLEAN.** Measured with python3 counting `b"\xc2\xa0"`: 0 NBSP in all

### 2.3 Tabs

Two tabs: **Invoice** and **Purchase Request**. Attested four times, in four files:

- "On the Delegate Configurations page, select either the Invoice or Purchase Request tab." (create-a-new-invoice-delegate-configuration-fcf42662.md) — emitted as `tabsSourceQuote`
- "Select the Invoice or Purchase Request tab." (access-and-view-payment-delegate-configurations-8ed1298f.md)

⚠ The `access-and-view` variant of this sentence is the one Run A briefly mis-assigned to
the Workflows Approval Statuses sub-tabs. That correction is already recorded in the built
`page.workflows` node. Do not re-open it.

### 2.4 THE IDENTITY QUESTION THE RECON DID NOT SETTLE: the child window

**DECISION: it is a MODAL ON THIS PAGE, not a separate page node.**

The corpus gives FIVE names for ONE surface across FOUR files — a grounded label-drift
contradiction that should itself be emitted:

| name | file |
| --- | --- |
| "Choose New. The Add Delegate Configuration - Invoice page appears." | create-a-new-invoice-delegate-configuration-fcf42662.md |
| "in the Add Delegate Configuration window" / "This window is available by clicking ..." | delegate-experience-8b30fb06.md |
| "Select Modify. The Modify Delegate Configuration page appears." | edit-an-invoice-delegate-configuration-c7f51424.md |
| "This is also a link to the Edit Delegate Configuration page" | access-and-view-payment-delegate-configurations-8ed1298f.md |
| "Restrict approvers to those with equal or higher authorized approver limit setting to the Add Delegate Configuration page." | delegate-configuration-8b2bd26d.md (revision history) |

And a sixth, singular, for the parent itself: "Select Save to return to the Delegate
Configuration page." (create-a-new-invoice-delegate-configuration-fcf42662.md).

**The argument.** The word "page" is proven non-discriminating in this corpus: it covers
real pages AND the Workflows General / Steps / Step Rules wizard that this graph already
ruled is NOT a page, while `page.authorized-approval-limits` IS a page node and its own
nav quote says "window appears". So decide on STRUCTURE, three tests:

1. **Own menu destination?** No. The only path is `... > Delegate Configurations > New
   (or Modify)` — through the parent, never from a menu. (Authorized Approval Limits also
   lacks one, so this test alone is not decisive — hence tests 2 and 3.)
2. **Own role gate?** No. Nothing in the corpus gates the child differently from the parent.
   (Authorized Approval Limits sits under a different admin parent entirely —
   Administration > Company > User Administration — with no other home for its fields.)
3. **Own object model?** **No, and this is decisive.** The child window edits the *same*
   object the parent page lists, and the corpus documents the *same controls twice*: the
   parent's 11-column read-only table in
   `access-and-view-payment-delegate-configurations-8ed1298f.md` and the child's 6-row
   entry form in `create-a-new-invoice-delegate-configuration-fcf42662.md` are the same
   settings under different labels (Can Prepare ↔ Delegate can prepare; Can Approve
   Temporary ↔ Delegate can approve during specified period; Restrict Delegates to Group ↔
   Restrict delegate selection to user's group; Need Approver Role to Approve ↔ Require
   approver role for approval delegation; Name ↔ Configuration Name). A separate page node
   would duplicate every field in the graph and split one object across two homes.

That is the Workflows-wizard pattern (modal over an object → not a page), not the
Authorized Approval Limits pattern (a surface with no other home → a page). **Emit the
fields on `page.delegate-configurations`, noting that they are entered in the Add/Modify
Delegate Configuration modal and displayed read-only as list columns on the Invoice and
Purchase Request tabs.** Emit the five-name drift as a contradiction node so the label
mapping is not lost.

Note the symmetry: Email Reminders has the identical three-name child ("Email Reminder
window" / "Add Email Reminder page" / "Edit Email Reminder page") and gets the identical
ruling. One rule, applied twice, in the same run.

### 2.5 Role gate — DOCUMENTED ABSENCE

**There is no documented role gate for this page anywhere in this corpus.** Measured:
`grep -rn "Delegate Configuration"` across both directories, filtered for
role/administrator/permission language, returns only field-description prose. The 40-odd
`permissions-*.md` topics are per-guide boilerplate ("A company administrator may or may
not have the correct permissions to use this feature") and name no role. The nearest
role-shaped sentences are NOT gates and must not be recorded as such:

- "The Configuration administrator can restrict the delegates based on the following choices:" (create-a-new-invoice-delegate-configuration-fcf42662.md) — describes who uses a *field*, not who reaches the page.
- "The Invoice Admin sets this option when defining delegates." (delegate-experience-8b30fb06.md) — "Invoice Admin" here is the menu alias, not a role name.

`roleGates: []` is the correct, publishable answer. Do NOT complete the pattern by
borrowing the Invoice Configuration administrator role from a neighbouring page — that is
exactly the invented-value defect this build has already paid for twice.

### 2.7 The dangling endpoint `dep.g1.059` — report, do not contort

`dep.g1.059` points at `{page: "Delegate Configurations", field: "Delegate Configuration"}`
with the cardinality quote "Each group within your company can only have one Invoice
delegate configuration." Its target field name is **label-shaped**, not a field name — the
LABEL-vs-NAME trap. This run will emit `configuration_name` (label "Configuration Name")
and `name`, never a field literally called "Delegate Configuration". **The edge will not
auto-resolve. Report the mismatch for a correction pass; do not rename a field to force
it.** The cardinality itself is real and worth a dependency into the built
`page.group-configurations`.

fields.name: restrict_approvers_to_equal_or_higher_authorized_approver_limit
fields.label: Restrict approvers to those with equal or higher authorized approver limit

fields.name: delegate_settings_for_user_administrators_and_employees
fields.label: Delegate Settings For User Administrators and Employees
fields.sourceQuote: In this section, you can select any or all of the following options for both the user and the administrator:
fields.notes: SECTION HEADING, NOT A SETTABLE CONTROL. Row 6 (the last) of the editor roster; its Description cell holds the nested FIVE-ENTRY bullet catalogue that is the heart of this page (emitted separately as delegate_can_prepare / delegate_can_submit / delegate_can_approve_any_time / delegate_can_approve_during_specified_period / delegate_can_view_images, and enumerated in valueSetCandidates). 'any or all' establishes that the five are INDEPENDENT multi-select checkboxes, not a radio group. 'for both the user and the administrator' is the permission-subset model from overview-8b2ba917.md: 'The user or the User Administrator share identical sets of permissions that are available when either of them assigns a delegate, as defined in the delegate configuration.' - i.e. there is exactly ONE set of five checkboxes, not two, and the editor topic is explicit that 'There is no option to provide separate permissions for specific employees or by their assigned roles.' Do not model a per-role duplicate of these five.  || REPAIRED (containment, not values), per refuter 2's named defect. The tables lens emitted a valueSetCandidate keyed appliesToField 'delegate_settings_for_user_administrators_and_employees' whose values were this row's FIVE CHILD CONTROLS ('Delegate can prepare', 'Delegate can submit', 'Delegate can approve (any time)', 'Delegate can approve during specified period', 'Delegate can view images'). All five are already emitted as FIELDS on this page, so wiring that set would double-book five controls - once as fields, once as values of their own parent. RECLASSIFY as a containment / child list or DROP; do not wire it as validValues. validValues stays [] and fieldType stays 'unknown' because this row is a SECTION HEADING, not a settable control. The two structural facts are preserved above: 'any or all' establishes FIVE INDEPENDENT checkboxes rather than a radio group, and the permission-subset model plus 'There is no option to provide separate permissions for specific employees or by their assigned roles.' means there is exactly ONE set of five - do NOT model a per-role duplicate for the User Administrator.

THE ARGUMENT. The word 'page' is proven non-discriminating here - it covers real pages AND the Workflows General/Steps/Step Rules wizard already ruled NOT a page, while page.authorized-approval-limits IS a page node and its own nav quote says 'window appears'. So decide on STRUCTURE, three tests. (1) Own menu destination? NO - the only path is through the parent, '... > Delegate Configurations > New (or Modify)'. Not decisive alone, since Authorized Approval Limits also lacks one. (2) Own role gate? NO - nothing gates the child differently from the parent, whereas Authorized Approval Limits sits under a wholly different admin parent (Administration > Company > User Administration) with no other home for its fields. fields.label: Reminder Rule
fields.sourceQuote: Use the Reminder Rule helper to select a previously created email reminder rule for the selected Reminder Type.
fields.notes: Selects among rules created on the Rules tab (the rule_name object), filtered by the Reminder Type selected above; not enumerable as a static value set - its population is dynamic (whatever rules exist for the chosen type, including the 2 system-supplied default rules named on Pre-Defined Rules). 'The Email Reminder Rules section of this tool is used to create any new rules.' Hard ordering: a rule must exist before a reminder can select one here - see dependencyCandidate rule-precedes-reminder. fields.name: frequency
fields.label: Frequency
fields.sourceQuote: Select how often you want this email to be sent once a rule is violated:
fields.notes: Email Reminders tab field. Controls conditional visibility of Number of Days (only if Every x days) and Specific days (only if Specific days of the month) - see dependencyCandidates. 'Once condition is met' carries a documented flag-reset caveat: flags are cleared every 60 days for performance reasons, so a once-only reminder can effectively repeat every 60 days unless the rule itself adds a time- or status-based guard condition.

fields.name: number-of-days
fields.label: Number of Days
fields.sourceQuote: This field appears only if you selected Every x days in the Frequency field.
fields.notes: Conditionally visible: only if Frequency = 'Every x days'. 'Enter the number of days since the last email reminder that this email is to be sent.' Behavior note: 'An email will be sent initially once the condition is met, then every “x days” as specified.'

fields.name: specific-days
fields.label: Specific days
fields.sourceQuote: This field appears only if you selected Specific days of the month in the Frequency field.
fields.notes: Conditionally visible: only if Frequency = 'Specific days of the month'. 'Enter a valid integer between 1 and 31. Use > for the last day of the month.' Example: '10, 20, > in the field would run the reminder on the 10th, 20th, and the last day of the month.' See compressedRange 'valid integer between 1 and 31'.

pages.verifyNotes:
ASSEMBLY RESULT: 26 inputs in (25 keep + 1 repair), 26 records out, 0 dropped, 0 split. Every record was pulled PROGRAMMATICALLY out of extract-email-reminders-procedure.json with python3 - no quote was retyped by hand. Both refuters gave verbatimVariantIndex 0 on all 26 candidates and agreed with each other; variant 0 is the procedures-and-controls record in every case, and the procedures lens is also the only lens carrying all 26 names (the tables lens has 18, all underscore-spelled; the crosscut lens emitted zero fields, correctly). I re-verified all 26 sourceQuotes myself with grep -F -c against the cited file: ALL 26 RETURNED EXACTLY 1. Zero misses, zero wrong-directory paths, no record carries the CONCUR_INVOICE/ prefix that broke an earlier drop pass.

THE ONE REPAIR - reminder-rule. Defect named by refuter-1: fieldType 'dropdown' asserted a widget the corpus never names. Fixed to 'unknown' (the value the tables lens already had). The only description in the source is 'Use the Reminder Rule helper to select a previously created email reminder rule for the selected Reminder Type.' - a HELPER - and the same file treats 'Helper pane' as a separate widget for Email Subject / Email Message. A Chromium driver told 'dropdown' would hunt for a select element that the documentation does not describe. sourceQuote, sourceFile, label, validValues ([] - the population is dynamic) and fromRawHtmlTable are unchanged and the quote re-verifies at 1. The repair is described in the record's own notes, along with the secondary item refuter-1 asked for: the two system-supplied seed rules from pre-defined-rules-220a1fe7.md are recorded there as a SEED population for the merger to wire as a value set, explicitly NOT as the field's complete option list.

NOTHING WAS SPLIT, ON PURPOSE. Refuter-2 finding 9 is right that New, Modify and Remove are each attested on BOTH tabs and that the graph's own precedent elsewhere (page.audit-rules CustomRuleModifyButton vs ValidationRuleModifyButton) splits per object. But records created during Repair never face the adversarial refuter, and mis-assignment is exactly what grep cannot catch, so all three stay as single best-grounded records whose notes already quote and attribute both tab behaviours. The three splits are reported in splitsProposed for the human instead. Rule-side quotes for them are grep -F verified and available: 'If they do not have permissions, then the New button will not appear.' (create-reminder-rules-b0a7fac5.md, 1 hit), 'Select the rule to edit, and then choose Modify.' (edit-reminder-rules-8f2edae9.md, 1 hit), 'Select the rule to delete, and then choose Remove.' (delete-reminder-rules-ab4f8d33.md, 1 hit). NOTE for whoever executes a split: the rule-side New step reads 'Choose New' with NO trailing period (line 29), so 'Choose New.' returns 0 against that file - do not copy the reminder-side punctuation across.

NAME HYGIENE, CHECKED AGAINST THE BUILT GRAPH (23 pages / 617 fields, read with python3 not assumed). No record pair in this roster shares a name - 26 unique. page.email-reminders does NOT yet exist in the graph, and no built field id contains 'email-reminder', so there is no page to collide with. The three within-page collisions the brief warned about are resolved exactly as instructed: rule_name / rule_reminder_type / rule_editable_by are prefixed, name / reminder-type / editable-by stay bare, and each of the six carries its tab in notes. They are NOT merged - the two Reminder Type option lists genuinely disagree and that disagreement is this run's strongest grounded contradiction. Cross-page reuse of bare labels (name, active, frequency, save-button and the rest) is the graph's own convention: field ids are page-prefixed, and the validator scopes duplicate-field-name PER PAGE.

THE WORKFLOWS COLLAPSE GUARD HELD, AND I RE-CHECKED IT RATHER THAN TRUSTING IT. field.workflows.email-notification-display-as-from and field.workflows.email-subject exist in the built graph but are sourced to modify-an-email-notification-a6e5f4ba.md / add-an-email-notification-c237a2de.md. Every record in this roster cites a reminder file instead; not one cites a notification file. Same labels, different files, different pages, different objects - Notifications are event-driven templates assigned to a workflow object, Reminders are interval-driven and assigned by GROUP. DO NOT DEDUPE THIS ROSTER BY LABEL AT MERGE TIME. Likewise no field was re-emitted from the six already-mined corroboration files.

BLIND-BUILD GUARD, RE-VERIFIED ON THE HIGHEST-RISK RECORD. 'active' carries validValues ['Yes'] ONLY. The corpus writes 'Select Yes to make this email reminder active. All email reminders are inactive by default.' and never names a 'No' for that control; the pair is deliberately NOT completed. copy-to-approver and copy-to-employee carry ['Yes','No'] and both sides are separately attested in create-email-reminders-604c4a46.md. editable-by and rule_editable_by carry ['Global Group'] only, correctly stopping short of the tenant hierarchy examples ('Global Group' + NBSP + 'United States') - which are also the NBSP hazard, so no quote in this roster crosses a U+00A0 sequence.

THREE THINGS THE MERGER MUST DO THAT ARE OUTSIDE THIS FILE'S SHAPE (this roster carries fields only):
1. WIRING DEFECT, MERGE-BLOCKING (refuter-2 finding 5 - this is the '17 sets landed unwired' defect in the making). The tables lens wires its value sets to reminder_type, reminder_rule, copy_to_approver, copy_to_employee, editable_by, email_message and the crosscut lens wires dependencies to applies_to, email_subject, email_message, reminder_rule, reminder_type. NONE of those underscore spellings is canonical. The canonical reminder-side names are the hyphenated ones in this file. Normalise every appliesToField and dependency target to hyphens before merge or those sets land on nothing. The rule-side names (rule_name / rule_reminder_type / rule_editable_by) are already canonical and must NOT be hyphenated.
2. THE 4-TOKEN SET (refuter-1 observation 1, refuter-2 findings 6 and 7). Both lenses propose NEW token sets; the graph already holds vset.g3.unnamed.email-message-replacement-tokens-the-4-row-variable-label-na with exactly ['%1%','%2%','%3%','%4%'], appliesToRef {page:'',field:'',resolved:false}, an EMPTY sourceQuote, and a note whose own stated fix is 'an Email Reminders page node that owns this table properly'. I confirmed that node's shape by reading the graph. RE-HOME it onto field.email-reminders.email-message; do not mint a second set. It needs a real quote and a verbatim one is available: 'You must type the variables manually.' (email-message-replacement-tokens-c9cc4af4.md, grep -F -c = 1). Do NOT put the 4-token set on email-subject: the corpus excludes one token there - 'This variable is not supported in the Email Subject field.' (same file, grep -F -c = 1). Correct shape is %1%/%2%/%3%/%4% on Email Message, %1%/%2%/%3% on Email Subject with the %4% exclusion recorded as a constraint. Leave page.purchase-order-configuration's own reference to that file alone.
3. NOTES MUST SURVIVE THE MERGE INTACT. Three real controls (the Rules-tab New, the rule-side Modify, the rule-side Remove) exist only inside the notes of new-button / modify-button / remove-button. If the merger truncates notes, those three lose their evidence entirely.

Select Remove.' which returns grep -F -c = 0 - it concatenates two separate numbered steps. display-as-from's notes render EmailReminderService@concursolutions.com as bare text inside quote marks where the file has a markdown mailto link, also 0. A driver cannot click it; it belongs in the graph as a dependency into the unbuilt Import/Extract Administrator surface. Same shape for localisation string extraction. (b) THE 'CONDITIONS - STEP 2' CONDITION EDITOR IS THIN BY EVIDENCE, NOT BY EFFORT. create-reminder-rules-b0a7fac5.md step 5 names Data Object, Field/Value and Operator in PROSE ONLY - no field table, no operator list, no data-object list anywhere for reminders. The operator and data-object catalogues in the-condition-page-5d4ea870.md and the-query-builder-and-the-condition-editor-e10473f9.md are the AUDIT RULES condition editor, already mined by that page, and the corpus NEVER says the two editors are the same. They were not imported. Thin is the correct answer here and it stays thin. (c) The two pre-defined rules are named with their 7-day trigger conditions but have NO documented configuration surface - whether they can be edited, copied or deleted is UNDETERMINED. (d) The reminder object has no documented Copy control at all: copy-email-reminders-cb75f9fd.md step 3 reuses Modify while the rule side correctly says 'Select the rule to copy, and then choose Copy.' No reminder-side Copy button was invented. (e) Reminder delete documents no confirmation dialog; rule delete does - confirm-yes-button is scoped to rule delete only.

The gate is real but NOT distinct: grep -rln "Invoice Configuration administrator (Restricted)" over BOTH guide dirs returns exactly 9 files, so it gates nine surfaces.

*** NBSP HAZARD - READ BEFORE TOUCHING THE NAV STRINGS ***
Two of the sentences that name Administration contain NO '>' glyph at all; the separators are two consecutive U+00A0. Measured with python3 counting b'\xc2\xa0':
  - access-email-reminders-96f3ca18.md (2 NBSP), step 1 reads: Select Administration<U+00A0><U+00A0>Invoice.
  - email-reminders-tool-8b2c8a11.md (2 NBSP), role sentence reads: The Email Reminders tool, located in Administration<U+00A0><U+00A0>Invoice, allows a Global and Group Configuration administrator to create, edit, and delete email reminders by group.
  - create-email-reminders-604c4a46.md (14) and create-reminder-rules-b0a7fac5.md (14) carry theirs inside the Editable By descriptions (Global Group<U+00A0><U+00A0>United States), not in a nav sentence.
bin/validate-graph.py NORMALISES NBSP to a space before comparing, so a retyped quote passes and lands permanently wrong - a nav string a Chromium driver can never match. I measured my own emission fidelity against these two files twice and it was NOT reliable (same intent produced U+00A0 once and U+0020 once). So I deliberately did NOT emit either full sentence. Instead the first nav segment is attested by the boundary-truncated verbatim 'Select Administration' (grep -F verified, 1 hit, cut exactly where the first U+00A0 begins), the alternate path by 'The Email Reminders tool, located in Administration' (1 hit), and the role by the ASCII-clean tail 'allows a Global and Group Configuration administrator...'. A CORRECTION PASS THAT CAN WRITE BYTES DIRECTLY SHOULD REPLACE THESE THREE WITH THE FULL SENTENCES ABOVE, inserting U+00A0 U+00A0 where this note writes <U+00A0><U+00A0>. Do not retype them by hand. The byte-exact sentences are in the survey file at the wroteTo path.

(create-email-reminders-604c4a46.md); 'Below is an example of how those options are used on the Add Email Reminder page.' The tables lens wired it to appliesToField 'configuration_name' (the Configuration Name text box); the Delegate Configurations roster explicitly DETACHED it and instructed 'DROP OR RE-SCOPE, DO NOT WIRE', for a reason worth preserving: nine label-drift aliases were collapsed on this page in the roster pass (Can Prepare -> delegate_can_prepare, Can Submit -> delegate_can_submit, Can Approve/(Any Time) -> delegate_can_approve_any_time, Can Approve Temporary -> delegate_can_approve_during_specified_period, Can View Images -> delegate_can_view_images, Restrict Delegates to Group -> restrict_delegate_selection_to_users_group, Need Approver Role to Approve -> require_approver_role_for_approval_delegation), and wiring this list as a text box's values would resurrect all of them as VALUES of an unrelated control. Reported here with page and field empty ON PURPOSE. TWELVE STRINGS, ELEVEN COLUMNS: 'Can Approve' and '(Any Time)' are ONE column whose label SAP splits across two lines inside a single markdown cell; no verbatim joined form exists in the file and joining them would fabricate text, so both fragments are listed and '(Any Time)' is NOT a twelfth column. The lead-in sentence, verbatim, is 'The following table describes the information that is displayed on either the Invoice or Purchase Request page by default.' CENSUS TRAP: SAP indents this table inside a numbered step, so a census anchored on '^|' returns ZERO on this file and the table is invisible to it. THIN FINDING WORTH PUBLISHING: this roster is the ONLY documentation the Purchase Request tab gets anywhere in the corpus - not one control is separately attributed to it, and the Invoice roster must NOT be mirrored onto it. WHAT WOULD FIX IT: A node type this graph does not currently have: a LIST-VIEW COLUMN ROSTER attached to the page (or to its tab strip, field 'tab-selector'), rather than to any single field. Failing that, leave it as a knownGap set - it is genuinely useful to a driver reading the list view and it must not be discarded, but it must never be materialised as any field's validValues.

Require approver role for approval delegation
valueSets.notes: ACCEPTED GAP - deliberately unwired. WHY NO OWNER: THIS IS A CONTAINMENT LIST, NOT AN OPTION LIST, AND IT MUST NOT BE WIRED AS VALUES. Both members are ALREADY EMITTED AS FIELDS on this page (restrict_delegate_selection_to_users_group and require_approver_role_for_approval_delegation), so attaching this to the parent row 'restrictions' - which the tables lens did - would double-book two real controls, once as fields and once as values of their own parent. The Delegate Configurations roster named that defect and ruled: 'RECLASSIFY as a containment / child list or DROP; it must not be wired as validValues.' Reported here rather than dropped so the grouping survives for a driver that needs to locate the two checkboxes. Lead-in sentence, verbatim: 'The Configuration administrator can restrict the delegates based on the following choices:' - and note that this names who USES the control, not who may reach the page; this page has NO documented role gate anywhere in the corpus. NEITHER MEMBER'S ON/OFF VALUES ARE DOCUMENTED: the corpus describes each only as 'If active, ...' and never names the opposite state, so no Yes/No pair may be completed for either. CROSS-READING: the same two controls appear on the read-only list view under different labels, 'Restrict Delegates to Group' and 'Need Approver Role to Approve'. WHAT WOULD FIX IT: A containment / parent-child edge (section heading -> member fields), which this graph's schema does not express as a value set. With that edge, this record disappears entirely and nothing is lost. Until then it stays an unwired knownGap set carrying the grouping.

valueSets.notes: ACCEPTED GAP - deliberately unwired. WHY NO OWNER: CONTAINMENT LIST, NOT AN OPTION LIST - same ruling as the Restrictions section above. All five members are ALREADY EMITTED AS FIELDS on this page, so wiring this to the parent row 'delegate_settings_for_user_administrators_and_employees' would double-book five real controls. The roster named the defect and ruled 'RECLASSIFY as a containment / child list or DROP'. Two structural facts the source states and that must not be lost: 'In this section, you can select any or all of the following options for both the user and the administrator:' establishes FIVE INDEPENDENT checkboxes, not a radio group; and 'for both the user and the administrator' does NOT mean two sets of five - overview-8b2ba917.md states the user and the User Administrator 'share identical sets of permissions', and this same topic states 'There is no option to provide separate permissions for specific employees or by their assigned roles.' ONE set of five. NO ON/OFF VALUES ARE DOCUMENTED for any of the five ('If active, ...' only), so no pair may be completed. CROSS-PAGE, DO NOT RE-HOME: the already-built page Workflows owns field.workflows.allow-delegated-approvers-to-approve-own-requests, and admin-guides/delegate-self-approval-1b627285.md describes that same control - it is a Workflows field and stays there; nothing from it is emitted here. WHAT WOULD FIX IT: The same containment / parent-child edge type. Until it exists, this stays an unwired knownGap set so the grouping - which a Chromium driver needs in order to find the five checkboxes under their heading - is not silently discarded.

dependencies.condition: RULE BEFORE REMINDER - the load-bearing ordering on this page. A reminder rule (Rules tab) must exist before the Reminder Rule field on the Email Reminders tab can be filled, unless one of the system default rules is used. configuration-process-8b2c271f.md orders the same sequence as numbered steps: step 1 'Create the rules: On the Rules tab of the Email Reminders page...' then step 2 'Create the configuration: On the Email Reminders tab of the Email Reminders page, create a new configuration.'
dependencies.sourceQuote: You must set up the rules before creating the email reminder, or you must use one of the default rules that the system provides.

dependencies.condition: Second, independent statement of the same ordering, at the level of the reminder configuration object itself (whose identity field is Name on the Email Reminders tab) rather than the Reminder Rule picker. The escape hatch is the same: a default rule removes the need to author one first.
dependencies.sourceQuote: A rule must be created before you create an email reminder, however, you can use one of the default rules.

dependencies.condition: OPTION-LIST dependency: the set of rules offered in Reminder Rule is filtered by the Reminder Type selected immediately above it. Reminder Type must therefore be set first.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Only the rules with this reminder type will appear in the next field.

dependencies.condition: CROSS-TAB, same page: the Reminder Rule helper offers only rules previously created on the Rules tab whose own Reminder Type (rule_reminder_type) matches the Reminder Type chosen on the Email Reminders tab. This is the rule-side half of the same filter; it is also a second statement that the rule must already exist.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Use the Reminder Rule helper to select a previously created email reminder rule for the selected Reminder Type.

dependencies.condition: CONDITIONAL VISIBILITY: Number of Days is rendered only when Frequency is set to 'Every x days'. A driver must set Frequency before this field exists.
dependencies.sourceQuote: This field appears only if you selected Every x days in the Frequency field.

dependencies.condition: CONDITIONAL VISIBILITY: Specific days is rendered only when Frequency is set to 'Specific days of the month'. A driver must set Frequency before this field exists.
dependencies.sourceQuote: This field appears only if you selected Specific days of the month in the Frequency field.

dependencies.condition: Frequency is an interval measured from the violation of the selected reminder rule, not an absolute calendar setting - the rule is what starts the clock, so the rule must be chosen for Frequency to mean anything.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Select how often you want this email to be sent once a rule is violated:

dependencies.condition: CONDITIONAL VISIBILITY, and the quote sits in the Copy to Approver row rather than the Copy to Employee row of the same field table: Copy to Employee is described as appearing only when the reminder is an approval invoice, which is determined by the Reminder Type selected (the two Approval Request types). The Copy to Employee row itself documents the control unconditionally, so the corpus is not fully consistent about whether the field is always present.
dependencies.sourceQuote: If the email reminder is an approval invoice, then the Copy to Employee setting appears, and the email is also sent to the employee for whom the invoice is requiring approval.

dependencies.condition: CONTENT dependency: which record fields the generated message body lists is determined by the reminder rule type, so the same Email Message text yields different content per Reminder Type. The token guide calls it 'Reminder Rule Type'; the Email Reminders tab field is labelled 'Reminder Type'.
dependencies.sourceQuote: The list of records for each Reminder Rule Type contain the following information in the email message:

dependencies.condition: DESTRUCTIVE SIDE EFFECT, cross-tab: removing a rule on the Rules tab flips the Active state of any Email Reminders tab configuration bound to it. The reminder record survives but stops sending until a new rule is selected.
dependencies.sourceQuote: If a rule is deleted that is currently associated with an email reminder, it will deactivate the email reminder.

dependencies.condition: THE SCHEDULING HANDOFF - the single most important thing a driver can be told about this page. Nothing on Email Reminders schedules anything: Frequency only describes the interval at which an already-scheduled job may send. A CONFIG WRITER CANNOT COMPLETE THIS LEG - scheduling is done in the Import/Extract Administrator tool by SAP Concur staff, and configuration-process-8b2c271f.md adds 'Scheduling requires you to submit a service request to SAP Concur support.' FORWARD REFERENCE into an UNBUILT surface: the Import/Extract Administrator is not modelled in this graph, and the corpus names no control on it for this job - the target field name is descriptive, not a documented label.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Scheduling email reminders is done in the Import/Extract Administrator tool and is performed by SAP Concur staff.

dependencies.condition: Companion to the scheduling handoff, and the practical rule for a driver: a NEW reminder configuration needs no new schedule - it joins the existing one. The schedule leg is required only the first time ('If this is the first time you create email reminder configurations, you must set up the schedule to run the email reminders.'). FORWARD REFERENCE into an UNBUILT surface; the target field name is descriptive, not a documented label.
dependencies.sourceQuote: The new email reminder will run on the same email reminder schedule that was set up prior.

dependencies.condition: GROUP-LEVEL ASSIGNMENT: a reminder is scoped by picking groups in Applies to, and those group objects are created and configured on the built Group Configurations page - which names email reminders explicitly as one of the things groups exist to differentiate. The groups must exist there before this field can bind to them. On this page the effect is exclusive, not inherited: 'Only the groups that you select will have this reminder available to them. The groups below the selected groups do not have this reminder available.'
dependencies.sourceQuote: Group Configurations within the Invoice Configuration administrator are used to identify and configure the groups necessary to provide employees with different payment policies, audit rules, email reminders, and vendors.

dependencies.condition: Editable By is expressed entirely in terms of the group hierarchy maintained on Group Configurations - the selectable entries are groups, and an administrator may only select groups at or beneath their own level ('Depending on your rights, you may not be able to select Global Group. You are only allowed to select groups beneath you.'). The hierarchy must exist before this field can be set.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Select the group rights that an administrator must have to modify this reminder.

dependencies.condition: Subject and message text entered here are NOT translated by the system. For multi-language groups the strings must be extracted and sent to a localization vendor, which 'may' require a service request to SAP Concur support - so, like scheduling, a config writer cannot complete this leg from this page. FORWARD REFERENCE into the UNBUILT Localization surface (Group 6); the corpus names no control for the extraction, so the target field name is descriptive, not a documented label.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Email Subject and Email Message text is not localized in the system automatically.

dependencies.condition: CROSS-GROUP TIMING COORDINATION, documented as a RECOMMENDATION rather than a system-enforced rule: a reminder rule aimed at a workflow step that times out should fire before the timeout elapses, so the rule's timing has to be derived from the workflow step's timeout duration. NOTE the naming drift already recorded in this graph: about-vendor-approval-workflow-step-and-timeout-b3d1bd2c.md calls the control 'Workflow Step Timeout Duration', which the Workflows page records as an alias/contradiction for the Approval Time Expired Action + Expire After This Many Days pair on the General page.
dependencies.sourceQuote: it would be helpful to create an email reminder for the Vendor Manager that triggers ~2 days prior to time out

dependencies.condition: THE DELEGATE / AUTHORIZED-APPROVER CROSS-REFERENCE. When this checkbox is selected, the delegate pool for an Authorized Approver is filtered against the Approval Limit values maintained on the Workflows > Authorized Approvers tab, so those limits must be loaded there before the restriction has anything to compare. Corroborated verbatim on the list-page roster in access-and-view-payment-delegate-configurations-8ed1298f.md.
dependencies.sourceQuote: If selected (enabled), the user selected to be a delegate for an Authorized Approver must also be an Authorized Approver, with the same or higher approver limit.

dependencies.condition: CLEARING the restriction has an active consequence, not a neutral one: for a delegate whose own authority is only for a lower approval limit, the approval permissions are withdrawn. The doc names the permissions by their list-page labels ('Can Approve' / 'Can Approve Temporary'); the editor labels them 'Delegate can approve (any time)' and 'Delegate can approve during specified period'.
dependencies.sourceQuote: When this setting is cleared (disabled), and a delegate with authority only for a lower approval limit is chosen, approval authority and functionality (Can Approve and Can Approve Temporary) become unavailable for that delegate

dependencies.condition: Second half of the same withdrawal: 'Can Approve Temporary' is the list-page label for the editor's 'Delegate can approve during specified period'. Same quote, same table row.
dependencies.sourceQuote: When this setting is cleared (disabled), and a delegate with authority only for a lower approval limit is chosen, approval authority and functionality (Can Approve and Can Approve Temporary) become unavailable for that delegate

dependencies.condition: EVALUATION TIMING, and it is a trap for a config writer: the limit comparison is made once, at delegate assignment. Later edits to the Amount on Authorized Approval Limits do NOT re-evaluate or revoke an existing delegate, and neither user nor delegate is notified ('If an Authorized Approver has the same or higher limit and becomes a delegate and if the Authorized Approver delegate's limit is later lowered, Concur Invoice does not remove that delegate nor is the user or delegate notified.'). So the limits must be correct BEFORE delegates are assigned.
dependencies.sourceQuote: The Authorized Approver limits are evaluated only when the delegate is assigned.

dependencies.condition: INFERRED: the corpus does not state this ordering against the delegate checkbox. What it states is that the Authorized Approver table is consulted only when the Workflows > Authorized Approvers configuration setting is on; since this restriction is defined entirely in terms of Authorized Approvers and their limits, it has nothing to evaluate on a site where that feature is off.
dependencies.sourceQuote: If the system is set to use the Authorized Approver table through the Workflows, Authorized Approvers page, Authorized Approver feature is available for workflows setting.

dependencies.condition: AUTHORITY INHERITANCE: granting approval here does not give the delegate their own authority - while acting on behalf of an authorized approver the delegate runs on that approver's limits, currencies and exception authority. What this checkbox actually controls is therefore bounded by values maintained on Authorized Approval Limits.
dependencies.sourceQuote: When a delegate is acting on behalf of an authorized approver, the delegate inherits the authority of that authorized approver, including that authorized approver's limits (if any), currencies, and exception authority (if any).

dependencies.condition: Same inheritance stated against LEVEL rather than limit: the delegate uses the original approver's Level from the Workflows > Authorized Approvers list, never their own. A delegate's own level is irrelevant to what they can approve on someone else's behalf.
dependencies.sourceQuote: The delegate approver acting on behalf of the assigned approver will use the level or limit rights assigned to the original approver rather than their own values.

dependencies.condition: DELEGATE SELF-APPROVAL: granting approval authority here does not settle whether a delegate may approve a request they themselves created on behalf of the approver - that is decided per workflow by the General-step setting on the built Workflows page. NOTE for the graph's integrity: delegate-self-approval-1b627285.md describes that SAME Workflows control and is deliberately NOT used to emit a field on Delegate Configurations.
dependencies.sourceQuote: This setting lets a company allow or prevent delegates to self-approve invoices that they create on behalf of an Approver

dependencies.condition: INTRA-PAGE GATE: ticking an approval permission does not by itself produce an approving delegate when the Restrictions checkbox is active - the selected delegate must additionally hold the Approver role, or delegate approval status is refused.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Require approver role for approval delegation: If active, the delegates assigned to this configuration must be assigned the Approver role in order to be allowed delegate approval status.

dependencies.condition: The role must already be held by the prospective delegate - it is not granted from this page. FORWARD REFERENCE into an UNBUILT surface: approver-terminology-8559861c.md places the grant elsewhere ('An Approver is set within User Permissions.'), and this corpus defers the user-profile surface to external Shared guides that are absent here - a DOCUMENTARY gap, not a menu-location one.
dependencies.sourceQuote: the delegate must already have the Invoice Approver role.

dependencies.condition: The restriction is evaluated against the employee group hierarchy maintained on the built Group Configurations page, so group membership there decides who an employee may pick as a delegate. Related trap documented in special-considerations-for-delegate-configurations-8b2bfccb.md: moving an employee to another group does not remove or update existing delegate assignments.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Restrict delegate selection to user's group: If active, the delegates assigned to this configuration can only act on behalf of another employee within their group.

dependencies.condition: CARDINALITY, one-to-one: a group carries at most one Invoice delegate configuration, so binding this configuration to a group displaces any other. The group objects are created on the built Group Configurations page and must exist first. This is also the honest endpoint for the dangling Group 1 edge dep.g1.059, which carries this exact quote but names a LABEL-shaped target field 'Delegate Configuration' that no field in this run is called - see the run notes.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Each group within your company can only have one Invoice delegate configuration.

dependencies.condition: The Inheritance toggle propagates this configuration down the employee group hierarchy defined on Group Configurations, so what it reaches is decided by that hierarchy and not by anything on this page. It is a toggle: 'The Inheritance link works as a toggle. When selected, the link switches between Inheritance and No Inheritance.'
dependencies.sourceQuote: Select the Inheritance link to apply the configuration to all groups that fall below the selected group in the hierarchy.

dependencies.condition: The admin sets the ceiling in days; the actual delegation dates are picked elsewhere, in the Delegates area of My Info and User Administration. FORWARD REFERENCE into an UNBUILT surface (the User Administration user profile, deferred to external Shared guides absent from this corpus). Restated verbatim on the list-page roster in access-and-view-payment-delegate-configurations-8ed1298f.md, there introduced by 'NOTE:' rather than a Note block.
dependencies.sourceQuote: This field works in conjunction with the Choose Dates link in the Delegates area of both My Info and User Administration.

dependencies.condition: INFERRED: the corpus does not state this ordering. It follows from the two rows describing the same quantity from opposite ends - this permission is the one that carries 'a set length of time', and Maximum Time Period to Approve is the only control on the page that expresses a time period in days. Treat the ceiling as configured before the permission is granted.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Delegate can approve during specified period: If active, the delegates assigned to this configuration can approve invoices on behalf of another employee. There is a set length of time associated with this action.

dependencies.condition: EXPLICIT TWO-STAGE ORDERING, stated by the corpus: the administrator grants the permission in the delegate configuration FIRST, and only then can it be conferred when the delegate is added for the employee. The employee can still withhold it ('This means an administrator may grant this ability, but the user can deny it when they add their delegate.'), so this page sets the ceiling, never the outcome. FORWARD REFERENCE into the UNBUILT User Administration / My Info delegate surface.
dependencies.sourceQuote: only if that permission was granted first within the delegate configuration by the User Admin, and then when the delegate was added for the employee.

dependencies.condition: Same ceiling-not-outcome pattern: the configuration permits image viewing, and the employee may override it per delegate on the Invoice Delegates page (Profile > Profile Settings > Invoice Delegates). FORWARD REFERENCE into the UNBUILT user-profile delegate surface. LABEL DRIFT worth noting for a driver: this same checkbox is called 'Delegate can view invoice images for payment requests' in delegate-experience-8b30fb06.md and 'Delegate can view images' in the create-configuration field table.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Although the configuration allows a delegate to view invoice images, the employee can elect to override this setting.

dependencies.condition: THE CASCADE, and it governs the whole permission block: every permission a user can grant or deny for their own delegate must first be allowed at the administrator level here. Configure this section before any per-employee delegate work is attempted. FORWARD REFERENCE into the UNBUILT User Administration / Profile delegate surface.
dependencies.sourceQuote: That is, the set of permissions available to a user to allow or deny are each allowed or disallowed at the administrator level.

steps.name: Configure an interval-driven email REMINDER end to end (group -> Rules tab rule -> Email Reminders tab configuration -> schedule -> optional localization)
steps.goal: An interval-driven nag email actually reaches a group of employees when a documented condition stays unresolved. THIS IS NOT THE WORKFLOWS EMAIL NOTIFICATIONS FLOW COVERED BY grpworkflows-s4: that step authors an event-driven NOTIFICATION template inside the Workflows page and selects it on a workflow object; this step authors a REMINDER on the separate Email Reminders page, which has its own two-tab rule engine, its own Frequency control, and is assigned BY GROUP rather than to a workflow. Four things half-work if a leg is skipped: (a) skip the Rules tab leg and the Reminder Rule helper on the Email Reminders tab has nothing to select, because the corpus states a rule must exist first (the only escape is one of the two system-supplied default rules); (b) set Reminder Type after picking a rule and the rule list is filtered by the wrong type, so the rule you wanted is simply not offered; (c) leave Active unset and the whole configuration sits there looking complete while sending nothing, because all reminders are inactive by default; (d) finish everything on this page and stop - nothing ever fires, because the SCHEDULE that runs reminders is not a control on this page at all and cannot be clicked by any administrator or driver.

sequence.action: confirm the group (or groups) this reminder will be scoped to already exists in the group hierarchy, creating it here if it does not
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: the reminder's Applies to and Editable By fields at orders 21-22 are populated from the site's own group tree, and that tree is built on this page - "Group Configurations within the Invoice Configuration administrator are used to identify and configure the groups necessary to provide employees with different payment policies, audit rules, email reminders, and vendors." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/overview-8b2edfd0.md). If the group does not exist yet, orders 21-22 have nothing correct to select and the reminder ends up scoped to the wrong slice of the company. ROLE GATE, and it is a real partition rather than a formality: "The Group Configurations tool is not visible if you have the Invoice Configuration administrator (Restricted) role." (same file), while the reminder page itself is reachable under exactly that role - "The Email Reminders tool is visible if you have the Invoice Configuration administrator (Restricted) role." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/email-reminders-tool-8b2c8a11.md). So an operator holding only the Restricted role can do orders 2-24 but CANNOT do this one and must have the group prepared by someone else.

sequence.action: reach the page from Administration > Invoice, then on the Rules tab choose New to open the New Reminder Rule - Step 1 page
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED ORDERING, attested three independent times, and it is the load-bearing fact of this whole procedure: "A rule must be created before you create an email reminder, however, you can use one of the default rules." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configuring-email-reminders-8b2c3cca.md); "You must set up the rules before creating the email reminder, or you must use one of the default rules that the system provides." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/before-you-begin-448d2513.md); and as step 1 of the documented process, "Create the rules: On the Rules tab of the Email Reminders page, create any specific email rules for the reminder or use one of the default rules." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configuration-process-8b2c271f.md). Run this leg out of order and the reminder has nothing to fire on. ACCESS IDIOM, recorded exactly as this page's own topic states it and NOT copied from the Delegate Configurations idiom: "From the Invoice Processing Admin navigation menu, choose Email Reminders." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/access-email-reminders-96f3ca18.md), then "On the Email Reminders page, select the Rules tab." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-reminder-rules-b0a7fac5.md). ROLE GATE on this specific click, verbatim: "If they do not have permissions, then the New button will not appear." (same file) - a driver that cannot find New on the Rules tab is looking at a rights problem, not a navigation problem. SKIPPABLE ONLY IF the two system-supplied default rules suffice; in that case jump to order 8.

sequence.action: type the rule name on the New Reminder Rule - Step 1 page
sequence.rationale: INFERRED from the roster ordering of the Step 1 page (Name, Reminder Type, Editable By, in that table order in concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-reminder-rules-b0a7fac5.md) plus the instruction "Complete all required fields." in the same procedure. The corpus states no uniqueness or length constraint for this control, so none is asserted here. NAMING HAZARD FOR A DRIVER: this control's on-screen label is 'Name', identical to the reminder-side 'Name' at order 9; they are different objects on different tabs and must not be conflated.

sequence.action: select the rule's Reminder Type
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, and this is why it must be set BEFORE the Next at order 6 rather than after: "Selecting a type also filters the options available when creating the rule using the condition editor on the next page." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-reminder-rules-b0a7fac5.md). Choose the type late and the Step 2 condition editor offers the wrong field/operator population. CONTRADICTION A DRIVER MUST BE TOLD: this Rules-tab list and the Email Reminders-tab list at order 10 genuinely disagree in this corpus - this file names 'Approval Request - Payment Vendor' where the reminder-side file names 'Approval Request - Vendor Request', and the two files define 'Approval Request - Payment Request' incompatibly. Both lists are recorded; neither is corrected against the other. Match this rule's type to whatever the reminder-side control at order 10 actually offers at runtime, because that is what filters the rule list at order 11.

sequence.action: select the group rights an administrator must hold to modify this rule
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: "Select the group rights that an administrator must have to modify this rule." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-reminder-rules-b0a7fac5.md). Ordering consequence rather than a mere preference: this is set while the rule is being authored, and the same file states that an administrator without rights to every selected group "can only be viewed and copied" - so an over-narrow selection here locks the rule against the very people expected to maintain it, and the mistake is only discoverable later. Only 'Global Group' is a corpus-fixed option; everything else in the list is the tenant's own group tree and is deliberately not enumerated.

sequence.action: choose Next to reach the Conditions - Step 2 page and build the rule condition from the Data Object, Field/Value and Operator helper panes
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: "Choose Next." then "Select the appropriate Data Object." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-reminder-rules-b0a7fac5.md). The condition is what makes the rule mean anything - a rule with no condition gives the reminder nothing to detect. This is also the step that consumes the type-filtering set at order 4, which is the reason order 4 cannot be deferred until after this click.

sequence.action: select Finish to commit the rule and return to the Rules tab
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: "Select Finish." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-reminder-rules-b0a7fac5.md). Load-bearing because the rule object does not exist until the wizard is committed, and the Reminder Rule helper at order 11 can only select an existing rule - "Use the Reminder Rule helper to select a previously created email reminder rule for the selected Reminder Type." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-email-reminders-604c4a46.md) - so an abandoned wizard leaves order 11 with nothing to pick. Note the rule wizard commits with Next/Finish and has NO Save control; the reminder object at order 24 commits with Save and has no Finish. Do not cross the two.

sequence.action: select the Email Reminders tab and choose New to open the Email Reminder window
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: "In Email Reminders, select the Email Reminders tab." then "Choose New to open the Email Reminder window." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-email-reminders-604c4a46.md). The tab switch is the boundary between the two objects this page owns: everything at orders 2-7 configured a RULE; everything from here configures a REMINDER that consumes one. A driver that stays on the Rules tab will find none of the fields below.

sequence.action: type a unique name for the reminder configuration
sequence.rationale: INFERRED from the row order of the Email Reminders configuration-fields table in concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-email-reminders-604c4a46.md, under that procedure's instruction to complete the required fields. The corpus does state uniqueness for this one ("Type a unique name for the email reminder configuration."), unlike the rule-side Name at order 3, which says only "Type a name" - a real asymmetry between the two tabs, not an editing slip to smooth over.

sequence.action: select the Reminder Type this reminder applies to
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, and it is a hard gate on the next control, not a categorisation nicety: "Only the rules with this reminder type will appear in the next field." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-email-reminders-604c4a46.md). Set this to the wrong type and the rule authored at orders 3-7 is simply absent from the Reminder Rule helper at order 11, with no error - the classic silent half-configuration on this page. See the contradiction noted at order 4: this file's option list differs from the Rules-tab file's list, and both are recorded rather than reconciled.

sequence.action: use the Reminder Rule helper to select the rule this reminder fires on
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED dependency on orders 2-7: "Use the Reminder Rule helper to select a previously created email reminder rule for the selected Reminder Type." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-email-reminders-604c4a46.md) - previously created, and filtered by the type set at order 10. INFERRED WIDGET CAUTION for a Chromium driver: the corpus calls this a 'helper' and never a dropdown, list or modal, so the element type must be resolved at runtime rather than assumed to be a select. Its population is dynamic (the tenant's own rules for the chosen type, plus the two system-supplied default rules) and is therefore not enumerable from documentation.

sequence.action: select how often the email is sent once the rule is violated
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, and it must precede orders 13-14 because it is what makes them exist at all: "This field appears only if you selected Every x days in the Frequency field." and "This field appears only if you selected Specific days of the month in the Frequency field." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-email-reminders-604c4a46.md). A driver that looks for Number of Days before setting Frequency will not find it. INFERRED CAUTION on the 'Once condition is met' option: the same file documents that the underlying flags are cleared periodically for performance, so a reminder intended to fire once can repeat unless the RULE authored at orders 2-7 carries its own time- or status-based guard - i.e. a Frequency choice made here can silently push work back onto order 6.

sequence.action: if and only if Frequency is 'Every x days', enter the number of days since the last reminder
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED conditional visibility, gated by order 12: "This field appears only if you selected Every x days in the Frequency field." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-email-reminders-604c4a46.md). Skipping the leg is correct when Frequency is anything else; attempting it out of order is a guaranteed element-not-found.

sequence.action: if and only if Frequency is 'Specific days of the month', enter the day numbers
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED conditional visibility, gated by order 12: "This field appears only if you selected Specific days of the month in the Frequency field." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-email-reminders-604c4a46.md). The accepted input is a compressed range documented as a valid integer between 1 and 31, with > standing for the last day of the month - a driver must not normalise the > away.

sequence.action: type the display name recipients will see as the sender
sequence.rationale: INFERRED from the table row order in concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-email-reminders-604c4a46.md. CONSTRAINT WORTH CARRYING: the @ symbol is not permitted in this name, and the file states the value affects the display name only, never the underlying sending address - so an operator who sets this expecting replies to route somewhere new has misread the control. DISAMBIGUATION: an identically-labelled 'Display as From' already exists in the graph on the Workflows page's Email Notifications tab; that is a different object on a different page and this step must not be run against it.

sequence.action: type the email subject line, typing any replacement tokens manually
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED constraint that changes how the step must be driven: "You must type the variables manually." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/email-message-replacement-tokens-c9cc4af4.md) - the tokens cannot be inserted by selecting from the Helper pane, so a driver must emit literal text such as %3%. Second corpus-stated constraint, and the reason this field is not interchangeable with order 17: "This variable is not supported in the Email Subject field." (same file) applies to the %4% List of Records token, so Subject carries three usable tokens where Message carries four. Maximum 255 characters.

sequence.action: type the email body, again typing any replacement tokens manually
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: same manual-typing rule as order 16, and this is the only field where %4% (List of Records) works. The 2,000-character limit counts double-byte characters as two, which is what ties this field to the optional localization leg at order 26 - text that fits in English can overflow after translation, and the corpus states plainly that "Email Subject and Email Message text is not localized in the system automatically." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/localizing-email-reminder-text-8b2cc1b0.md). INFERRED: author the final wording here before requesting extraction at order 26, or the strings sent for translation are the wrong ones.

sequence.action: select whether a copy goes to the employee's default approver
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, and it gates the control at order 19: setting Yes on an approval invoice is what makes Copy to Employee appear - "If the email reminder is an approval invoice, then the Copy to Employee setting appears" (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-email-reminders-604c4a46.md). Both Yes and No are documented for this control in prose, so both are recorded; that is not true of Active at order 23.

sequence.action: if it appeared, select whether a copy also goes to the employee the pending item belongs to
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED conditional appearance, gated by order 18.
