PRIVACY CONSEQUENCE a config writer must weigh before ticking it, from the same file: when several items are pending one approver, every relevant employee is added as a cc recipient and can therefore see information about other employees' items. This is a decision, not a default - and it is unrecoverable once the mail is sent.

sequence.action: type any additional recipient addresses, separated by comma or semicolon
sequence.rationale: INFERRED from the table row order in concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-email-reminders-604c4a46.md; the separator rule (comma or semicolon) is corpus-stated in the same row and is the only documented formatting constraint.

sequence.action: select the group rights an administrator must hold to modify this reminder
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: "Select the group rights that an administrator must have to modify this reminder." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-email-reminders-604c4a46.md). Depends on order 1: the groups offered here come from the group hierarchy. Ordering consequence: the same file states an administrator lacking rights to every selected group can copy the reminder but not edit or delete it, so an over-narrow selection made now is a lockout discovered later by someone else.

sequence.action: select the groups that will have this reminder available to them
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, and the inheritance direction is the trap: "Select the groups that will be able to see this reminder." followed by "The groups below the selected groups do not have this reminder available." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-email-reminders-604c4a46.md). This is the OPPOSITE of the Editable By behaviour at order 21, where rights do inherit downward - so an operator who assumes one rule for both fields will scope the reminder to a fraction of the intended audience and see no error. This assignment-by-group is also the axis that distinguishes this page from the Workflows Email Notifications tab, which assigns to a workflow object instead.

sequence.action: set Active to Yes
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, and it is the single most common way this configuration silently half-works: "Select Yes to make this email reminder active. All email reminders are inactive by default." and "Emails are not sent until you set this field to Yes." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-email-reminders-604c4a46.md). Placed last among the field entries because everything above should be correct before the reminder is allowed to send. BLIND-BUILD NOTE for the driver: only the value 'Yes' is documented for this control - the corpus never writes a 'No' option for it, so do not synthesise one.

sequence.action: choose Save to commit the reminder and return to the Email Reminders list
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: "Choose Save." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-email-reminders-604c4a46.md), after which the reminder appears in the list. The reminder object commits with Save; the rule object at order 7 commits with Finish. Two different commit idioms on one page.

sequence.action: STOP - a config writer cannot complete this leg. If this is the site's first email reminder configuration, raise a service request to SAP Concur support to have the email reminder schedule established; if reminders already run on this site, do nothing here
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, and stated as an out-of-band handoff rather than a control: "Scheduling email reminders is done in the Import/Extract Administrator tool and is performed by SAP Concur staff." and "Scheduling requires you to submit a service request to SAP Concur support." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configuration-process-8b2c271f.md). THERE IS NO SCHEDULING FIELD ANYWHERE ON THE EMAIL REMINDERS PAGE and no automation can click one - a driver that treats orders 1-24 as a completed configuration will report success on a reminder that never sends. The corpus also bounds when this is needed: "If this is the first time you create email reminder configurations, you must set up the schedule to run the email reminders." but "The new email reminder will run on the same email reminder schedule that was set up prior." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/scheduling-email-reminders-8b2ceaea.md) - so the escalation is once per site, not once per reminder. Target page is UNBUILT and unresolved on purpose.

sequence.action: OPTIONAL, and also not completable by a config writer. If the assigned groups span languages, raise a service request to SAP Concur support to extract the Email Subject and Email Message strings for translation by a localization vendor
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: "Email Subject and Email Message text is not localized in the system automatically." and "you may have to submit a service request to SAP Concur support for assistance with extracting the strings." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/localizing-email-reminder-text-8b2cc1b0.md). It sits after order 24 because the strings must exist and be final before they can be extracted. INFERRED consequence of skipping it: the reminder is fully functional and sends - in one language only - which is why this failure is invisible to any check that merely asks whether mail went out. Target page is UNBUILT and unresolved on purpose.

steps.name: Swap the rule behind a live email reminder without silently deactivating it (author replacement -> repoint the reminder -> only then remove the old rule)
steps.goal: A live email reminder is moved onto a new or corrected rule and keeps sending throughout. The ordering here is the entire point: the corpus documents a reverse cascade in which deleting a rule does not delete the reminders that used it but DEACTIVATES them, so the obvious sequence - tidy up the old rule first, then repoint - takes production reminders offline with no error and no notification, and the damage is only visible as mail that stopped arriving. Two further quiet failures: author the replacement rule under a different Reminder Type than the reminder uses and it never appears in the Reminder Rule helper at all; and repoint the reminder without re-checking Active and a reminder already deactivated by an earlier rule deletion stays silent even after it has a valid rule again.

sequence.action: on the Rules tab, choose New to open the New Reminder Rule - Step 1 page for the replacement rule
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED that the replacement must exist before anything is removed, because the reminder can only ever select an existing rule: "Use the Reminder Rule helper to select a previously created email reminder rule for the selected Reminder Type." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-email-reminders-604c4a46.md). Building the replacement first is also what keeps the old rule intact and the reminder sending while the swap is prepared.

sequence.action: name the replacement rule
sequence.rationale: INFERRED from the Step 1 roster order in concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-reminder-rules-b0a7fac5.md. INFERRED OPERATIONAL POINT: give it a name distinguishable from the rule being retired, because order 8 removes one of the two by selection from a list and the corpus documents no undo for that removal.

sequence.action: set the replacement rule's Reminder Type to the same type the target reminder uses
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, and this is the leg that most often makes the swap silently impossible: the reminder side filters its rule list by type - "Only the rules with this reminder type will appear in the next field." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-email-reminders-604c4a46.md) - so a replacement authored under a different type simply will not be offered at order 6, with no message explaining why. It must also precede the Next at order 4 because "Selecting a type also filters the options available when creating the rule using the condition editor on the next page." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-reminder-rules-b0a7fac5.md).

sequence.action: set the group rights required to modify the replacement rule
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: "Select the group rights that an administrator must have to modify this rule." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-reminder-rules-b0a7fac5.md). INFERRED ordering point: mirror whatever the retired rule carried, or the swap quietly changes who can maintain the rule afterwards - a governance regression hidden inside what was meant to be a like-for-like replacement.

sequence.action: choose Next, build the condition on the Conditions - Step 2 page, then select Finish
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: "Choose Next." and "Select Finish." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-reminder-rules-b0a7fac5.md). Load-bearing because an uncommitted wizard leaves no rule object at all, and order 6 then finds nothing new to select while the operator believes the replacement exists.

sequence.action: switch to the Email Reminders tab, select the live reminder and choose Modify to open the Email Reminder window, then confirm its Reminder Type
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: "Choose Modify to open the Email Reminder window." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/edit-email-reminders-2a2638ad.md). Reading the type back before touching the rule is what proves the replacement authored at order 3 will actually be offered - the check costs nothing and is the only way to detect the type mismatch before it presents as an empty helper.

sequence.action: in the Reminder Rule helper, select the replacement rule
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED as the documented recovery path as well as the swap itself: a reminder deactivated by a deleted rule is repaired by reopening it and selecting a new rule, which is exactly this entry. Doing it BEFORE order 9 is what prevents the deactivation in the first place - see the cascade quoted at order 9.

sequence.action: confirm Active is set to Yes, then choose Save
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: "Emails are not sent until you set this field to Yes." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-email-reminders-604c4a46.md). This is not redundant re-checking - if a rule deletion has already happened on this site the reminder is already deactivated, and repointing it alone will not resume sending. A driver that skips this entry can complete a technically correct swap on a reminder that stays silent forever.

sequence.action: commit the reminder with Save before going anywhere near the Rules tab
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: "Choose Save." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-email-reminders-604c4a46.md). This entry exists as its own order because an uncommitted Modify window means the reminder is still associated with the OLD rule, and the removal at order 10 would then hit the cascade the whole step is designed to avoid.

sequence.action: only now return to the Rules tab, select the retired rule and choose Remove
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, and this is the hazard that dictates the entire ordering of this step: "If a rule is deleted that is currently associated with an email reminder, it will deactivate the email reminder." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/delete-reminder-rules-ab4f8d33.md). Run this first and every reminder still pointing at the rule goes dark - the reminder records survive, so nothing looks deleted and nothing raises an error. The removal is safe only once no live reminder references the rule, which orders 7-9 guarantee. Control idiom: "Select the rule to delete, and then choose Remove." (same file).

sequence.action: in the confirmation message, select Yes
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: "In the confirmation message, select Yes to dismiss the message." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/delete-reminder-rules-ab4f8d33.md). DOCUMENTED ASYMMETRY a driver must be told about rather than allowed to generalise: rule deletion has this confirmation dialog, but reminder deletion in this corpus has none - "Select the email reminder you want to delete." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/delete-email-reminders-8f693700.md) is followed by Remove taking effect with no confirmation step described. An automation that waits for a confirm dialog on the reminder side will hang; one that assumes a safety net there has already deleted the record.

steps.name: Create an Invoice delegate configuration and cascade it down the group hierarchy (tab -> New -> permissions and restrictions -> Applies to Groups with Inheritance -> Save)
steps.goal: One group - and, through the Inheritance toggle, every group beneath it - has a delegate permission template that defines exactly what a delegate may do on another employee's behalf. What half-works if a leg is skipped: (a) the target group already holds a delegate configuration and the corpus permits only one per group, so a second attempt is a cardinality collision rather than an addition; (b) set the permission checkboxes but never touch the Inheritance link and the configuration stops at the selected group while every group below it silently keeps whatever it had, or nothing; (c) tick 'Delegate can approve during specified period' but leave Maximum Time Period to Approve at whatever it was and the ceiling on the delegation is not the one intended - and the actual dates are not settable on this page at all; (d) finish here and assume delegation is live - it is not: this page only defines the permission SUBSET, and the delegate is still assigned on another surface, where the employee can also refuse a permission the administrator granted.

sequence.action: confirm the target group exists and establish whether it - or any group above it that inherits downward - already carries an Invoice delegate configuration
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED CARDINALITY, and it is the reason this check comes first rather than being discovered at Save: "Each group within your company can only have one Invoice delegate configuration." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-invoice-delegate-configuration-fcf42662.md). Building a second configuration for a group that already has one is not an additive change. The check has to include groups ABOVE the target, because an inherited configuration from a parent group is already in force on the child. ROLE PARTITION worth flagging: "The Group Configurations tool is not visible if you have the Invoice Configuration administrator (Restricted) role." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/overview-8b2edfd0.md), whereas this corpus documents NO role gate at all on the Delegate Configurations page - so a Restricted-role operator may be able to do every remaining order and be unable to do this one.

sequence.action: reach the page from Administration > Invoice via the left menu, then select either the Invoice or Purchase Request tab
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, and recorded with THIS page's own access idiom rather than the Email Reminders one: "Select Delegate Configurations (left menu) , the Delegate Configurations page appears." then "Select the Invoice or Purchase Request tab." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/access-and-view-payment-delegate-configurations-8ed1298f.md); the create topic states the same tab choice as its own step 1, "On the Delegate Configurations page, select either the Invoice or Purchase Request tab." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-invoice-delegate-configuration-fcf42662.md). Whether the 'Invoice Processing Admin' middle node also appears in this path is UNATTESTED for this page and is not asserted. The tab must be chosen before New because it decides which object is created - and note the documentary asymmetry: every field below is documented for the Invoice side only, so a driver on the Purchase Request tab is off the map and must not assume the Invoice roster mirrors across.

sequence.action: choose New to open the Add Delegate Configuration window
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: "Choose New. The Add Delegate Configuration - Invoice page appears." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-invoice-delegate-configuration-fcf42662.md). Every field from order 4 down lives inside this window and does not exist before this click.

sequence.action: type the configuration name
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED and it is the ONLY control the corpus marks as mandatory on this page: "The name of the new delegate configuration. This is a required field." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-invoice-delegate-configuration-fcf42662.md). Everything else can be left alone and the record will still save, which is precisely why the permission checkboxes below fail quietly rather than loudly. INFERRED, worth knowing before naming it: in the list view this same value doubles as the hyperlink that opens the edit surface, so an unhelpful name is also a navigation problem later. No length, character-set or uniqueness constraint is documented, and none is invented here.

sequence.action: enter the maximum time period, in days, for which a delegate may approve on another employee's behalf
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED unit and purpose: "Indicates a set time period, in days, for which an employee can approve invoices on behalf of another employee." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-invoice-delegate-configuration-fcf42662.md). It is set BEFORE the temporary-approval checkbox at order 16 because it is the ceiling that checkbox operates under. HARD LIMIT ON WHAT THIS STEP CAN ACHIEVE, corpus-stated: "This field works in conjunction with the Choose Dates link in the Delegates area of both My Info and User Administration." (same file) - the actual start and end dates are chosen off this page, on surfaces this graph has not built, so setting a ceiling here delegates nothing on its own. No minimum, maximum or default is documented anywhere in the corpus and a blind build must not supply one.

sequence.action: locate the Restrictions section in the window
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED grouping, not a settable control: "The Configuration administrator can restrict the delegates based on the following choices:" (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-invoice-delegate-configuration-fcf42662.md). Recorded as its own order because a driver needs the container to find the two checkboxes at orders 7-8, and because an operator who reads this heading as a control will look for a value that does not exist. NOT a role gate - 'The Configuration administrator' here names who uses the field, and this corpus documents no role gate for reaching this page at all.

sequence.action: decide whether delegates may act only for employees inside their own group
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: "Restrict delegate selection to user's group: If active, the delegates assigned to this configuration can only act on behalf of another employee within their group." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-invoice-delegate-configuration-fcf42662.md). Ordering consequence that reaches beyond this window: existing cross-group delegate assignments are stripped automatically when an employee moves into a group whose configuration forbids them, so turning this on retroactively removes assignments elsewhere rather than merely constraining future ones. LABEL HAZARD: the same control is captioned 'Restrict Delegates to Group' in the list view and described there with the opposite polarity (whether delegates outside the group CAN be selected) - a driver must probe both captions and must not read the two sentences as two settings.

sequence.action: decide whether a delegate must already hold the Approver role before receiving delegate approval status
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: "Require approver role for approval delegation: If active, the delegates assigned to this configuration must be assigned the Approver role in order to be allowed delegate approval status." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-invoice-delegate-configuration-fcf42662.md). It is an ordering constraint on work done on ANOTHER surface: the role itself is granted in user permissions, not here, so ticking this before the intended delegates hold the role makes those delegates unassignable later. Corroborated as an unconditional prerequisite in the authorized-approver path: "the delegate must already be an approver, that is, the delegate must already have the Invoice Approver role." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/approver-terminology-8559861c.md). LABEL HAZARD: captioned 'Need Approver Role to Approve' in the list view.

sequence.action: decide whether a delegate for an Authorized Approver must themselves be an Authorized Approver with an equal or higher limit
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: "If selected (enabled), the user selected to be a delegate for an Authorized Approver must also be an Authorized Approver, with the same or higher approver limit." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-invoice-delegate-configuration-fcf42662.md). It must be settled BEFORE the approve checkboxes at orders 15-16, because clearing it changes what those checkboxes can deliver: "When this setting is cleared (disabled), and a delegate with authority only for a lower approval limit is chosen, approval authority and functionality (Can Approve and Can Approve Temporary) become unavailable for that delegate" (same file) - so the operator ticks an approve permission and that specific delegate still cannot approve. See grpworkflows-b4 for the full cross-page procedure.

sequence.action: select the group this configuration applies to in Applies to Groups
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED binding to the group prepared at order 1, under the one-per-group rule quoted there. INFERRED ordering point: choose the group before touching the Inheritance link at order 11, because inheritance is defined relative to the SELECTED group - "Select the Inheritance link to apply the configuration to all groups that fall below the selected group in the hierarchy." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-invoice-delegate-configuration-fcf42662.md). Toggling first and selecting after leaves the cascade anchored to the wrong node. The value space is the tenant's own group hierarchy and is deliberately not enumerated.

sequence.action: read the Inheritance link's current caption and toggle it until it reads the state you want
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, and the driver instruction is 'read, then decide' rather than 'click': "The Inheritance link works as a toggle. When selected, the link switches between Inheritance and No Inheritance." and "When Inheritance is displayed, the configuration is inherited by the groups below the selected group, in the hierarchy." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-invoice-delegate-configuration-fcf42662.md). This is the only enumerated option list on the entire page, and both captions are printed in the corpus - they are not a completed pair. Because the caption mutates with state, a blind click can set exactly the opposite of what was intended, and the mistake is invisible: the configuration saves either way and the difference only shows up as child groups that do or do not have delegation. Related but NOT proven identical to the Is Inheritable concept on Group Configurations; the corpus does not equate them and neither does this step.

sequence.action: locate the Delegate Settings For User Administrators and Employees section
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED grouping, not a settable control, and it carries two facts the following five orders depend on: "In this section, you can select any or all of the following options for both the user and the administrator:" (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-invoice-delegate-configuration-fcf42662.md). 'any or all' establishes these are INDEPENDENT checkboxes rather than a radio group, so a driver must not expect selecting one to clear another; 'for both the user and the administrator' establishes there is exactly ONE set of five, not a separate admin set and user set - the same file states there is no option to provide separate permissions by employee or role.

sequence.action: decide whether delegates may create invoices on another employee's behalf
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: "Delegate can prepare: If active, the delegates assigned to this configuration can create invoices on behalf of another employee." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-invoice-delegate-configuration-fcf42662.md). CONSEQUENCE OF LEAVING IT OFF that a config writer must plan for, because it is retroactive rather than merely forward-looking: "If the old delegate configuration had rights, such as Can Prepare, associated with it, but the new configuration does not allow prepare rights, then that delegate will no longer be able to prepare." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/special-considerations-for-payment-delegate-configurations-77a887a4.md). LABEL HAZARD: 'Can Prepare' in the list view, and the two descriptions use different verbs (create vs prepare) for one control.

sequence.action: decide whether delegates may submit invoices on another employee's behalf
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, and this is the control on which the two-gate model is made explicit - granting it here is NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT: a delegate may submit "only if that permission was granted first within the delegate configuration by the User Admin, and then when the delegate was added for the employee." and "This means an administrator may grant this ability, but the user can deny it when they add their delegate." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/delegates-submit-a-payment-or-purchase-request-0ee0f0b9.md). A driver that ticks this box cannot report that the delegate can submit - only that the first of two gates is open. This is why order 19 exists.

sequence.action: decide whether delegates may approve with no time limit
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: "Delegate can approve (any time): If active, the delegates assigned to this configuration can approve invoices on behalf of another employee." with the qualifier that there is no time period associated with the action (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-invoice-delegate-configuration-fcf42662.md). Gated by order 9 - with that restriction cleared and a lower-limit delegate chosen, this permission becomes unavailable for that delegate regardless of the tick here. LABEL HAZARD: the list view splits the caption across two lines as 'Can Approve' and '(Any Time)', so no single verbatim caption match will find it there.

sequence.action: decide whether delegates may approve only within a bounded period
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: "There is a set length of time associated with this action." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-invoice-delegate-configuration-fcf42662.md). Paired with order 5, which supplies the day ceiling, and dependent on a surface this step cannot reach for the actual dates. INFERRED, and it is the reason this pairing is called out rather than left implicit: ticking this box while the ceiling at order 5 is unconsidered produces a temporary delegation whose bound is not the one the operator has in mind, and nothing on this page will show the discrepancy. LABEL HAZARD: 'Can Approve Temporary' in the list view.

sequence.action: decide whether delegates may view invoice images
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: "Delegate can view images: If active, the delegates assigned to this configuration can view Invoice images for invoices on behalf of another employee." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-invoice-delegate-configuration-fcf42662.md). OVERRIDE a config writer must expect: even when allowed here, the employee can clear it per delegate on the end-user surface - "the Can View Images check box on the Invoice Delegates page by clicking Profile > Profile Settings > Invoice Delegates" (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/delegate-experience-8b30fb06.md). WORST LABEL DRIFT ON THE PAGE - three captions across three files ('Delegate can view images', 'Can View Images', and a longer modal caption about viewing invoice images for payment requests); a driver must probe all three.

sequence.action: select Save to commit the configuration and return to the parent list
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: "Select Save to return to the Delegate Configuration page." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-invoice-delegate-configuration-fcf42662.md). NOTE THE NAMING DRIFT rather than treating it as two destinations: the edit topic writes the same return target in the PLURAL ('the Delegate Configurations page'). One surface, two spellings.

sequence.action: assign the actual delegate to the employee - this page defined only the permission template, and the delegation does not exist until it is assigned here
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED that the assignment is a different surface, and that this page's output merely shapes it: "The columns that appear for the delegate will vary, depending on the settings in the delegates configuration file." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/invoice-user-f11cccd8.md). Combined with the two-gate quote at order 14, the consequence for a driver is blunt: completing orders 1-18 changes nothing about who can act for whom, and reporting the delegation as configured would be wrong. Target page is UNBUILT in this graph and this entry is unresolved on purpose - the corpus defers it to external Shared guides absent from this corpus, which is a documentary gap rather than a missing menu location.

steps.name: Enable delegation for Authorized Approvers (set the approver limits first, then gate the delegate configuration, and only then assign the delegate)
steps.goal: A delegate can approve on behalf of an Authorized Approver without either over-granting authority or being locked out of approving at all. The ordering is forced by a rule the corpus states plainly and that has no UI signal whatsoever: authorized approver limits are evaluated ONLY at the moment the delegate is assigned, and are never re-checked afterwards. So limits set after assignment are ignored, and a limit lowered after assignment leaves a delegate approving above their current authority with nobody notified. The other quiet failures: leave the equal-or-higher restriction cleared and the approve permissions granted on the delegate configuration silently become unavailable for any lower-limit delegate; and tick 'Require approver role for approval delegation' before the intended delegates hold the Invoice Approver role and they cannot be assigned at all.

sequence.action: mark the intended delegate as an Authorized Approver
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED prerequisite for the gate configured at order 7: "If selected (enabled), the user selected to be a delegate for an Authorized Approver must also be an Authorized Approver, with the same or higher approver limit." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-invoice-delegate-configuration-fcf42662.md). Do this after order 10 instead and the delegate simply fails the check at assignment time, because the check happens then and only then.

sequence.action: set the approval limit currency for that approver
sequence.rationale: INFERRED from the pairing of currency and amount on the built Authorized Approval Limits page: an amount without its currency does not describe a limit that can be compared against another approver's. CORPUS-STATED consequence that makes the comparison matter: a delegate acting for an authorized approver does not use their own values - "the delegate inherits the authority of that authorized approver, including that authorized approver's limits (if any), currencies, and exception authority (if any)." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/delegates-4d7c563c.md).

sequence.action: set the approval limit amount so it is equal to or higher than the limit of the approver being delegated for
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: the equal-or-higher comparison at order 7 is made against this number. Getting it wrong here does not raise an error on the Delegate Configurations page - it surfaces later as a delegate who cannot be assigned, or (with the restriction cleared) as one whose approve permissions quietly do nothing.

sequence.action: grant exception-approval rights if the delegated authority is meant to include them
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED that exception authority travels with the delegation and is not configurable on the delegate side: it is part of what "the delegate inherits" (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/delegates-4d7c563c.md). INFERRED ordering point: because it is inherited rather than granted per delegate, it must be correct on the approver record before assignment - there is no control on Delegate Configurations that can add or remove it afterwards.

sequence.action: save the approver record
sequence.rationale: INFERRED from the built page's own commit control, and load-bearing here for a specific documented reason: an uncommitted limit is not a limit, and the evaluation at assignment reads what is stored - "The Authorized Approver limits are evaluated only when the delegate is assigned." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-invoice-delegate-configuration-fcf42662.md). There is no second evaluation later to catch up with a save made after order 10.

sequence.action: open the Delegate Configurations page, select the Invoice tab and open the configuration that applies to the delegate's group with Modify (or create one as in grpworkflows-b3)
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: "Select Modify. The Modify Delegate Configuration page appears." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/edit-an-invoice-delegate-configuration-c7f51424.md), reached after the tab choice documented at concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/access-and-view-payment-delegate-configurations-8ed1298f.md. Modify rather than New, because the corpus permits only one Invoice delegate configuration per group - if one already covers this group, creating another is a collision, not an addition.

sequence.action: select the restriction requiring delegates of Authorized Approvers to hold an equal or higher limit
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, and this entry is the hinge of the whole step: with it set, the limits established at orders 1-5 are enforced at assignment; with it CLEARED, "a delegate with authority only for a lower approval limit is chosen, approval authority and functionality (Can Approve and Can Approve Temporary) become unavailable for that delegate" (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-invoice-delegate-configuration-fcf42662.md). Both outcomes look identical on this screen - the checkboxes at orders 9-10 can be ticked either way - and the difference only appears as a delegate who cannot approve. SILENT-DRIFT HAZARD, corpus-stated in the same note: if the delegate's limit is later lowered, Concur Invoice does not remove the delegate and neither the user nor the delegate is notified, so this configuration needs periodic re-checking that no control on this page provides.

sequence.action: select whether delegates must already hold the Approver role
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: "Require approver role for approval delegation: If active, the delegates assigned to this configuration must be assigned the Approver role in order to be allowed delegate approval status." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-invoice-delegate-configuration-fcf42662.md), and stated unconditionally for this path as "the delegate must already be an approver, that is, the delegate must already have the Invoice Approver role." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/approver-terminology-8559861c.md). It is an ordering constraint on work outside this graph: the role is granted in user permissions, not here, so setting this before the delegates hold the role makes them unassignable at order 12 with no explanation offered on this page.

sequence.action: grant unbounded approval if the delegation is intended to be open-ended
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED that this permission is conditioned on order 7 rather than independent of it - the same note states that "approval authority and functionality (Can Approve and Can Approve Temporary) become unavailable for that delegate" when the restriction is cleared and a delegate with only a lower approval limit is chosen (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-invoice-delegate-configuration-fcf42662.md). That is why order 7 precedes it: granting first and restricting afterwards produces a permission that reads as granted and behaves as absent.

sequence.action: grant bounded approval instead, and set the day ceiling it operates under
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: "There is a set length of time associated with this action." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-invoice-delegate-configuration-fcf42662.md), with the ceiling supplied by Maximum Time Period to Approve on the same window. INFERRED, and it is the reason this option is preferable for authorized-approver delegation specifically: because limits are evaluated only at assignment and never re-checked, a bounded delegation expires on its own, whereas an open-ended one persists through any later change to the approver's limit with nobody notified.

sequence.action: set or confirm the maximum time period in days, then save the configuration
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED ceiling and its off-page partner: "Indicates a set time period, in days, for which an employee can approve invoices on behalf of another employee." and "This field works in conjunction with the Choose Dates link in the Delegates area of both My Info and User Administration." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-invoice-delegate-configuration-fcf42662.md). The ceiling must be committed before order 12, because the dates chosen at assignment are bounded by it - set it afterwards and the delegation already in place is not the one intended. Commit with "Select Save to return to the Delegate Configuration page." (same file).

sequence.action: assign the delegate to the Authorized Approver, and choose the delegation dates via the Choose Dates link if bounded approval was granted
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, and it is the moment everything above is tested exactly once: "The Authorized Approver limits are evaluated only when the delegate is assigned." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-invoice-delegate-configuration-fcf42662.md). Any leg above left until after this point is not merely late - it is never evaluated. The dates themselves are corpus-stated to live here rather than on the admin page, per the Choose Dates quote at order 11, and the permission set the delegate ends up with is shaped by what was saved at order 11: "The columns that appear for the delegate will vary, depending on the settings in the delegates configuration file." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/invoice-user-f11cccd8.md). Target page is UNBUILT and this entry is unresolved on purpose. SCOPE BOUNDARY: whether a delegated approver may approve requests they created themselves is NOT set here and NOT on Delegate Configurations - it is the already-built Workflows control, "A setting, Allow delegated approvers to approve their own requests, is available in the General step." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/delegate-self-approval-1b627285.md).

contradictions.topic: The Reminder Type option list differs between the Email Reminders tab roster and the Rules tab roster of the same page, and the one option both lists share is defined incompatibly - a cash advance request on one side, an invoice on the other.

readings.summary: Email Reminders tab roster: the vendor option is spelled 'Approval Request - Vendor Request'.
readings.sourceQuote: Approval Request - Vendor Request: When a vendor-based invoice has a status of Pending Approval.

readings.summary: Rules tab roster: the same conceptual vendor option is spelled 'Approval Request - Payment Vendor' instead.
readings.sourceQuote: Approval Request - Payment Vendor: When a vendor-based invoice has a status of Pending Approval.

readings.summary: Email Reminders tab roster defines the SHARED option 'Approval Request - Payment Request' as firing on a CASH ADVANCE REQUEST that is Pending Approval.
readings.sourceQuote: Approval Request - Payment Request: When a cash advance request has a status of Pending Approval.

readings.summary: Rules tab roster defines the same shared option as firing on an INVOICE that is Pending Approval.
readings.sourceQuote: Approval Request - Payment Request: When an invoice has a status of Pending Approval.

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: Do not reconcile the two lists and do not pick one as authoritative. Probe BOTH label spellings for the vendor option: on the Email Reminders tab probe 'Approval Request - Vendor Request' first, on the Rules tab probe 'Approval Request - Payment Vendor' first, and fall back to the other spelling before concluding the option is absent - a substring match on 'Vendor' is the safe locator. Never identify 'Approval Request - Payment Request' from its description text, because the two topics disagree about what fires it; select it by label only. The third option, 'Payment Request', is uncontested on both sides. This matters operationally because a reminder can only use rules of its own Reminder Type, so a mismatch between the reminder-side picker (field reminder-type) and the rule-side picker (field rule_reminder_type) is a SILENT failure: the Reminder Rule helper simply returns nothing.
contradictions.notes: Both readings are single corpus hits in DIFFERENT files and both are recorded verbatim; neither is corrected. HYPOTHESIS, not a finding: the cash-advance definition looks like SAP boilerplate carried over from the Expense product, where cash advance requests are a first-class object - Concur Invoice has no documented cash advance surface anywhere else in this corpus. SECOND HYPOTHESIS: 'Approval Request - Payment Vendor' may be the live label, because the two system pre-defined rules are named 'Overdue Payment Request Approvals' and 'Overdue Payment Vendor Approvals' (pre-defined-rules-220a1fe7.md), echoing 'Payment Vendor' rather than 'Vendor Request'. That is CORROBORATION FOR ONE SIDE, NOT A RESOLUTION, and a blind build has no tenant to check it against. Textual tell that the two tables drifted in editing rather than describing two deliberately different pickers: their otherwise identical lead-in sentences differ by one word, 'activated upon' (reminder side) versus 'activated on' (rule side). Both topics carry the same version and build_no and neither carries any UI-variant language. The two pickers are carried in the roster as SEPARATE fields (reminder-type and rule_reminder_type); this node is filed against the reminder-side field and applies equally to the rule-side one.

contradictions.topic: The reminder editor opened from the Email Reminders tab is named three different ways across three topics of the same guide, and is called both a window and a page.

readings.summary: The create procedure calls it the 'Email Reminder window'.
readings.sourceQuote: Choose New to open the Email Reminder window.

readings.summary: The edit topic calls the read-only variant of the same editor the 'Edit Email Reminder page'.
readings.sourceQuote: If they do not have permissions, then the Edit Email Reminder page will be read-only.

readings.summary: The replacement-tokens topic calls the same editor the 'Add Email Reminder page'.
readings.sourceQuote: Below is an example of how those options are used on the Add Email Reminder page.

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: Treat 'Email Reminder window', 'Add Email Reminder page' and 'Edit Email Reminder page' as ONE modal editor over the reminder object and do NOT create page nodes for any of them - none has a menu destination, a role gate or an object of its own. Locate the editor by the New / Modify action that opens it, not by matching a title string; if a title assertion is unavoidable, match on the substring 'Email Reminder' in the container caption and expect the Add/Edit prefix to track whether New or Modify was chosen. Never branch logic on 'window' versus 'page'.
contradictions.notes: Hypothesis: three topics written at different times describe one UI container, and the Add/Edit prefix probably does vary at runtime with the entry point while 'window' versus 'page' is editorial drift. The word 'page' is PROVEN NON-DISCRIMINATING in this corpus - the graph already ruled the Workflows General/Steps/Step Rules wizard is not a page although the corpus calls it one, while page.authorized-approval-limits IS a page node and its own nav sentence says a window appears. The rules side of this page shows the same shape with a fourth name, 'The New Reminder Rule - Step 1 page appears.' (create-reminder-rules-b0a7fac5.md), and the edit procedure lands on that same 'New Reminder Rule - Step 1' caption (edit-reminder-rules-8f2edae9.md) even though nothing new is being created. appliesTo is deliberately empty: this is a page-level surface-naming disagreement, not a disagreement about any one control.

contradictions.topic: How a copy is initiated differs between the two tabs of this page: the Rules tab has a named Copy control, while the topic titled Copy Email Reminders names only Modify.

readings.summary: Rules tab: copying is done with an explicitly named Copy control.
readings.sourceQuote: Select the rule to copy, and then choose Copy.

readings.summary: Email Reminders tab: the topic titled 'Copy Email Reminders' names no Copy control anywhere - its only action step is Modify, the same control its own Edit topic uses.
readings.sourceQuote: Choose Modify to open the Email Reminder window and make any necessary changes.

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: On the Rules tab, drive Copy directly - it is documented. On the Email Reminders tab, do NOT invent or hunt for a Copy button: the corpus never attests one there, and completing the pair by assumption is exactly the blind-build defect this project has already paid for. Follow the documented path (select the reminder, Modify, change it, Save) and then VERIFY that a new entry appeared in the list rather than the original being overwritten, because the documented procedure as written produces an edit, not a copy. If a Copy affordance does turn out to exist at runtime on the reminders tab, report it as an undocumented finding rather than treating it as expected.
contradictions.notes: Hypothesis: a corpus defect rather than a real UI asymmetry - the copy-reminder topic reads as the edit topic with its title swapped, retaining 'Choose Modify' and 'Choose Save' and describing copying only in its closing line. Indirect support that a copy affordance exists on both objects: the Editable By description on BOTH tabs independently grants lower-level administrators a copy right, saying they 'can copy this reminder, but not edit or delete it' and 'can copy this rule, but not edit or delete it'. That is an inference and is NOT emitted as a control. Filed against the rule-side Copy button because that field's scope - whether a Copy control exists for one object or both - is exactly what is contested.

contradictions.topic: Who may administer Email Reminders is stated three incompatible ways, twice within a single topic: a Global and Group Configuration administrator, a Group Configuration administrator limited to their own groups, and the holder of the Invoice Configuration administrator (Restricted) role - with a further per-group 'create' rights gate named only on the CRUD topics.

readings.summary: The tool topic says the surface allows a Global and Group Configuration administrator to do the full CRUD, with Group Configuration administrators limited to the groups they have access to.
readings.sourceQuote: allows a Global and Group Configuration administrator to create, edit, and delete email reminders by group.

readings.summary: The SAME topic, two lines later, gates mere VISIBILITY of the tool on a differently-named role: Invoice Configuration administrator (Restricted).
readings.sourceQuote: The Email Reminders tool is visible if you have the Invoice Configuration administrator (Restricted) role.

readings.summary: The rule-creation topic adds a third gate that neither of the above mentions - a per-administrator 'create' right whose absence removes the New button entirely.
readings.sourceQuote: Group administrators can only create email reminder rules if given "create" rights. If they do not have permissions, then the New button will not appear.

readings.summary: The reminder-edit topic states the same 'create' rights gate for EDITING reminders, and sources the right from the Invoice Configuration administrator's configuration checklist rather than from a role.
readings.sourceQuote: Group administrators can only edit email reminders if given "create" rights from the configuration checklist of the Invoice Configuration administrator.

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: Do not treat any one of these as THE permission for this page. Before driving the page, establish all three independently: (a) that the operator holds a role that makes Email Reminders visible at all, probing 'Invoice Configuration administrator (Restricted)' and the Global/Group Configuration administrator names as alternatives, not synonyms; (b) that the operator's group scope covers the groups the reminder will be assigned to, since a Group Configuration administrator is documented as limited to their own groups; and (c) that the 'create' right is present, because without it the failure is SILENT AND SHAPE-CHANGING - the New button is absent on the Rules tab and the reminder editor opens read-only. A driver that finds no New button must report a rights gap, NOT a missing control or a changed layout.
contradictions.notes: Hypothesis: these are three different mechanisms (a role that grants visibility, a group hierarchy that scopes what is editable, and a checklist-granted create right) rather than three names for one thing - which would make all four sentences simultaneously true. THE CORPUS NEVER SAYS THIS and never relates them, so nothing is reconciled here. Note also that the edit topic sources 'create' rights from a configuration checklist while the rule topic just says 'if given "create" rights', and that the word used for the edit gate is 'create', not 'edit' - which reads like a copy from the create topic but is recorded as written. Verbatim-quote hazard measured in the first reading's sentence and the reason its quote starts mid-sentence: the source writes the menu path as 'Administration' + TWO NON-BREAKING SPACES (U+00A0 U+00A0) + 'Invoice', with no '>' character at all - a harder form of the documented 'Administration >Invoice' trap, and a quote spanning those bytes cannot be retyped safely, so the clause was cut before them. appliesTo is empty because this is a page-level access requirement, not a control.

contradictions.topic: The name of the restricted Invoice Configuration administrator role - the gate that makes the Email Reminders tool visible - is written three different ways across the corpus, and two of the three variants live in tools-guides.

readings.summary: Admin-guides, and this page's own gate sentence: the qualifier follows the full role name - 'Invoice Configuration administrator (Restricted)'.
readings.sourceQuote: The Email Reminders tool is visible if you have the Invoice Configuration administrator (Restricted) role.

readings.summary: Tools-guides, Company Locations: the qualifier moves INSIDE the role name, before the word administrator - 'Invoice Configuration (Restricted) administrator'.
readings.sourceQuote: users must be assigned the Invoice Configuration administrator or Invoice Configuration (Restricted) administrator role

readings.summary: Tools-guides, invoice assignment: a third spelling drops the word Configuration entirely - 'Invoice Administrator (Restricted)'.
readings.sourceQuote: the configuration of the feature requires the Invoice Administrator (Restricted) role

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: Treat all three spellings as the SAME role when checking whether the operator can see the Email Reminders tool, and never create a second role for a near-miss. When matching a role string in a permissions UI, probe 'Invoice Configuration administrator (Restricted)' first - it is this page's own spelling and the majority form - then 'Invoice Configuration (Restricted) administrator', then 'Invoice Administrator (Restricted)'. Do not report the role as absent until all three have missed.
contradictions.notes: Hypothesis: editorial drift across deliverables rather than a product distinction - the three spellings gate three unrelated features (Email Reminders, Company Locations, invoice assignment) and no text anywhere distinguishes them. Corroborating measurement made with equal weight on both guide directories: the exact string 'Invoice Configuration administrator (Restricted)' appears in NINE files (5 admin-guides, 4 tools-guides), so this gate is NOT distinctive to Email Reminders. A complementary form, 'Invoice Configuration administrator (Unrestricted)', appears in the Capture Processing required-roles topic, so the corpus does treat Restricted/Unrestricted as a real partition even while spelling the label inconsistently. This node is about the ROLE NAME only; who may do what on this page is contradicted separately and more sharply in contr.wfb.004.

contradictions.topic: What kind of object 'Invoice Processing Admin' is - the middle navigation node this page hangs off. The corpus calls it a navigation menu, a menu, and a page.

readings.summary: This page's own access topic calls it a navigation menu that you choose an item from.
readings.sourceQuote: From the Invoice Processing Admin navigation menu, choose Email Reminders.

readings.summary: Tools-guides, Routing Configuration: the same node is a plain 'menu' that you click an item on.
readings.sourceQuote: From the Invoice Processing Admin menu, click Routing Configuration.

readings.summary: Tools-guides, Invoice Settings: the same node is a PAGE you are already on when you click through.
readings.sourceQuote: On the Invoice Processing Admin page, click Invoice Settings.

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: Do not encode 'Invoice Processing Admin' as a clickable leaf destination and do not assume the driver lands on a page there. Treat it as a middle segment traversed after Administration > Invoice, and resolve the real target ('Email Reminders') by its own visible text. If a probe for a menu fails, retry treating the segment as a landing page carrying links. The segment is LIVE - it is attested in tools-guides files independently of this page's own topic - but it is NOT universal in this run: the Delegate Configurations access topic reaches its page by the plain '(left menu)' idiom and never names this segment, so treat the segment as UNATTESTED for that page rather than absent, and never copy one page's access idiom onto the other.
contradictions.notes: Hypothesis: the UI genuinely renders both - a left navigation menu and a landing page listing the same tools - and each topic describes whichever the author had open. This is NOT a UI-variant claim: none of the three files carries new-experience or legacy language, and no release note was used to date any of them. appliesTo is empty because this is a navigation-structure disagreement above the page, not a control on it.

contradictions.topic: Whether establishing the email-reminder schedule ALWAYS requires SAP Concur staff and a service request, or only depending on the client's implementation.

readings.summary: The configuration-process topic states it unconditionally: scheduling is done in another tool, is performed by SAP Concur staff, and requires a service request.
readings.sourceQuote: Scheduling requires you to submit a service request to SAP Concur support.

readings.summary: The dedicated scheduling topic makes it conditional on the client's implementation - you MAY have to submit a service request.
readings.sourceQuote: Depending on your company's implementation, you may have to submit a service request to SAP Concur support for assistance with this task.

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: Either way, scheduling is NOT a control on this page and must never be emitted as a field - a driver cannot click it. Build the reminder, then STOP and hand off. Do not report the configuration as live until it has been confirmed out of band that a reminder schedule already exists, because a correctly built reminder simply never fires without one and fails silently. Only the FIRST reminder configuration in a tenant needs the schedule established; later reminders inherit the existing schedule.
contradictions.notes: Hypothesis: provisioning-dependent, which is the standard cause of this shape in this corpus - some tenants may have the Import/Extract Administrator tool available to their own administrators, most do not. The two statements are not reconcilable from the docs and no tenant may be consulted to settle it. The Import/Extract Administrator tool is not built in this graph and is not a page for a driver to reach; it is listed among the deferred surfaces.

contradictions.topic: 'Rules tab' is not a unique locator in this product: it names the rules tab of the Email Reminders page and, equally, the rules tab of the Purchase Order matching rule set.

readings.summary: Email Reminders: the Rules tab is a tab of the Email Reminders page.
readings.sourceQuote: On the Email Reminders page, select the Rules tab.

readings.summary: Purchase Order matching: an identically-named Rules tab is a tab of the Purchase Order Matching Set, reached from a different page entirely.
readings.sourceQuote: In Purchase Order Matching Set, click the Rules tab.

readings.summary: Tools-guides confirms the same 'Rules tab' name on the matching side, independently of the admin-guides procedure.
readings.sourceQuote: Both options are available to the Invoice administration on the Rules tab when configuring the matching rule set.

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: A Chromium driver must never select the Rules tab by its caption alone. Always qualify it by the page it is on: assert you are on 'Email Reminders' before clicking Rules here, and on 'Purchase Order Matching Rules' (the built graph's page name for the matching surface) before clicking Rules there. Clicking an unqualified 'Rules' match is a cross-page misfire that will look like a successful step and then edit the wrong object.
contradictions.notes: Not a disagreement about one surface but a COLLISION between two: both readings are correct, and that is precisely the hazard. The Workflows area carries a near-neighbour, the 'Step Rules page' (work-with-the-step-rules-page-4c33cda0.md), whose caption is a different string and is therefore NOT recorded here as a third reading of the same label - it is noted only so a substring matcher on 'Rules' is understood to have a third way to go wrong. Cross-references use the exact built-graph page names Purchase Order Matching Rules and Workflows; no field or page is re-homed by this node.

contradictions.topic: The rules surface of the Email Reminders page is called the Rules tab in five topics and the 'Email Reminder Rules section of this tool' in the reminder-creation topic.

readings.summary: Five CRUD and process topics call it a tab of this page - here in the rule-creation procedure.
readings.sourceQuote: On the Email Reminders page, select the Rules tab.

readings.summary: The reminder-creation topic, describing where new rules come from, calls the same surface a SECTION of the tool rather than a tab.
readings.sourceQuote: The Email Reminder Rules section of this tool is used to create any new rules.

readings.summary: The prerequisites topic gives a third phrasing that locates the rules inside the page rather than naming a tab strip.
readings.sourceQuote: The rules are set up in the Rules tab of the Email Reminders page.

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: Probe the tab strip for the caption 'Rules' first - that is the form five separate topics use and the only one framed as a clickable tab. Accept an 'Email Reminder Rules' caption as the same surface if 'Rules' misses, and do not conclude the rules surface is absent from a single failed caption match. compressedRanges.label: a valid integer between 1 and 31
compressedRanges.sourceQuote: Enter a valid integer between 1 and 31. Use \> for the last day of the month.
compressedRanges.notes: MECHANICAL EXPANSION of an inclusive calendar day-of-month range; the 31 members are arithmetic, not enumerated by SAP, and that is stated here rather than hidden. SOURCE CHARACTERS: the range is written with the words 'between 1 and 31' and contains NO DASH of any kind, so there is no hyphen/en-dash hazard in the label; the '>' token is escaped in the source markdown as backslash-greater-than and the quote reproduces that backslash byte for byte, while the character a driver actually types is a bare '>'. THE '>' IS DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED FROM expandsTo: the source treats it as a separate token meaning the last day of the month ('Use > for the last day of the month.'), not as a member of the 1-31 integer range, and count must equal expandsTo length. The field accepts a COMMA-SEPARATED LIST of members rather than a single value - SAP's own worked example in the same cell is '10, 20, > in the field would run the reminder on the 10th, 20th, and the last day of the month.' UNDETERMINED and not inferred: whether duplicates, out-of-order lists, or 29/30/31 in a short month are accepted or rejected - the corpus is silent. The field appears only when Frequency is set to 'Specific days of the month', so a driver must set Frequency first or the control will not be present. Only ONE compressed range exists across this run's whole candidate file set: a scan for dash-ranges, 'between N and N' and 'Custom NN' patterns over both pages' topics returned this single hit, and the replacement-token variables %1% through %4% are ENUMERATED row by row in email-message-replacement-tokens-c9cc4af4.md, so they are correctly NOT a range node.

### 2a. FINDING (MEDIUM) — the `specific-days` value set is a redundant, *incomplete* copy of `range.wfb.001`

`synth-valuesets.json` → `valueSets[4]` and `synth-ranges.json` → `compressedRanges[0]` carry **the same
31 members, on the same field, from the same file, from the same sentence**. They are the same fact
written twice.

Worse, the value set is the *lossier* of the two. The source cell is:

```
create-email-reminders-604c4a46.md:138  This field appears only if you selected Specific days of the month …
create-email-reminders-604c4a46.md:140  Enter a valid integer between 1 and 31. Use \> for the last day of the month.
create-email-reminders-604c4a46.md:144  10, 20, > in the field would run the reminder on the 10th, 20th, and the last day of the month.
```

The field is a **free-text comma list**, and `>` is a documented, accepted, non-numeric input token.
`range.wfb.001` excludes `>` *and says so explicitly and correctly* (a sentinel is not a member of a
1–31 integer range, and `count` must equal `len(expandsTo)`). The value set excludes it with no such
guard. A Chromium driver reading `values` to decide what to type into **Specific days** will produce
`1..31` and **never produce `>`** — so "last day of the month" becomes unreachable, which is the single
most likely reason an admin picks this frequency at all.

**Fix (preferred):** drop `synth-valuesets.json` → `valueSets[4]`. The compressed range already carries
the expansion, is the correct node type for a prose range, and its notes carry `>`.
**Fix (alternative):** keep it but re-scope `context` to *accepted input tokens* and add `>` to `values`.
Do **not** add `>` to `range.wfb.001` — that would break `range-count-mismatch`.

Severity note: this is *not* a build-breaker. `value-set-entries-not-in-file` is a WARN, the baseline
graph already carries 11 of them (`python3 bin/validate-graph.py` → `WARN 181`), and the set's own notes
predict and justify the 12th. The defect is the redundancy plus the missing `>`, not the WARN.

### 9a. FINDING (HIGH, OPERATIONAL) — the merge invocation is the single thing that can destroy this graph, and it is not in the parts directory

Not a defect in the build artefacts — a precondition that must survive the handoff, because the failure
mode is silent and total. I simulated both invocations against the live graph:

```
gtag=workflowsw   intra-run duplicate ids: none   clashes with existing graph: 0
gtag=workflows    intra-run duplicate ids: none   clashes with existing graph: 53
                     e.g. contr.gworkflows.001 … dep.gworkflows.001 … range.gworkflows.001
```

`bin/merge-group.py:57` derives `gtag` from the group label; `:73` suffixes it with the patch-page
initials **only in patch mode**. So:

- **`--patch --patch-page "Workflows"`** → `gtag = workflowsw` → `dep.gworkflowsw.001…034`,
  `contr.gworkflowsw.001…018`, `range.gworkflowsw.001`. **Zero collisions.** In patch mode `touched` is
  `{page.email-reminders, page.delegate-configurations}`, neither of which is in the graph, so nothing
  existing is removed. This is the correct and safe path.
- **No `--patch`** → `gtag = workflows`, and `bin/merge-group.py:92-98` first executes
  `[x for x in … if x.get('group') != 'Workflows']` across **six** collections. That deletes Run A
  wholesale: 2 pages (`page.workflows`, `page.feature-hierarchies`), 121 fields, 61 dependencies,
  34 value sets, 24 contradictions, 5 compressed ranges, 7 steps — **and `validate-graph.py` then exits
  0 over the wreckage**, exactly as `merge-group.py:60-64` documents from the measured 2026-09-01 incident.
  The 53 id clashes never even surface, because the clashing nodes were deleted a moment earlier.

`workflows/2026-09-01_kg-workflows-run-b.mjs:12-31` already states this correctly. Restating it here
because the *critique* is what gets read at merge time, and because "validate-graph.py exits 0" is not
evidence that the merge was safe.
